# App management keywords

> Learn how to start, switch, close and inspect the app or browser under test.

App management keywords start and stop the app or browser that your test drives. Most suites call Launch App in a setup module and Close And Terminate App in a teardown module.

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2
Open Birch,Launch App,com.birch.shop
Close Birch,Close And Terminate App
```

See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/) for the rules all keywords share.

## Start and switch

### Launch App

Starts the app or browser under test, or brings the app to the front.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `app_identifier` | Empty | Appium: the Android package or iOS bundle id. Playwright and Selenium: the URL to open. Empty uses the app from your config. |
| `app_activity` | Empty | Appium on Android: the activity to start. Selenium: the browser name, `chrome` or `firefox`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. See [Event names](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#event-names). |

```csv
Open Birch,Launch App,com.birch.shop
Open Birch,Launch App,com.birch.shop,com.birch.shop.MainActivity
Open Birch Web,Launch App,https://birch.example
```

```yaml
- Launch App com.birch.shop
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, Launch App starts a session if none is running. If a session is already running and you give an identifier, it brings that app to the front.
- With no parameters, Launch App uses the app, URL and browser from your [config](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config).
- On Selenium, `app_identifier` and `app_activity` apply only when Launch App starts the session. Later calls reopen the configured URL.
- On Playwright, the browser is always Chromium in a visible 1280×800 window. The `browser`, `headless` and `viewport` capabilities are currently ignored.
- The BLE driver (a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse) can't launch apps. Open the app by tapping its icon instead.

### Start Appium Session

Starts a driver session without naming an app. It's the same as Launch App with no parameters, and it works with every driver despite its name.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Open Birch,Start Appium Session
```

### Launch Other App

Switches to another app, or opens a deep link or URL.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `app_name` | Required | An Android package, iOS bundle id, deep link or URL. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Share Product,Launch Other App,com.android.settings
Open Deep Link,Launch Other App,birch://product/trail-runner-2
Open Help,Launch Other App,https://birch.example/help
```

```yaml
- Launch Other App com.android.settings
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, a value containing `://` opens as a deep link or URL. Anything else is started or brought to the front as an app.
- On Playwright, the URL opens in a new tab.
- On Selenium, the current tab navigates to the URL.
- In Python the parameter is called `bundleid`.

## Close

### Close And Terminate App

Ends the driver session, which closes the app or browser, and sends any recorded events.

This keyword takes no parameters.

```csv
Close Birch,Close And Terminate App
```

```yaml
- Close And Terminate App
```

Good to know:

- After this keyword, later steps have no session. Put it in your last module or a teardown test case. See [Organise tests](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/organise).

### Force Terminate App

Kills a specific app.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `app_name` | Required | The Android package or iOS bundle id to kill. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Reset Birch,Force Terminate App,com.birch.shop
```

```yaml
- Force Terminate App com.birch.shop
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, errors are logged and the step passes, even if the app wasn't killed. With no session it does nothing.
- On Selenium, it closes the current browser window and ignores `app_name`.
- Playwright doesn't support it. The step fails.

## Inspect

### Get App Version

Reads the installed app's version.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `app_package` | Empty | The Android package or iOS bundle id. Empty uses the app from your config. |

```csv
App Info,Get App Version,com.birch.shop
```

Good to know:

- On Android, Optics reads the version through adb. On iOS, it uses ideviceinstaller, which must be installed.
- The CSV and YAML runner can't store the version in a variable. The value is returned over `optics serve`, MCP and [Python](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/python).
- Selenium doesn't support it, so the step fails. On Playwright it returns a "not supported" message, and passing `app_package` fails the step.

### Get Driver Session Id

Returns the id of the current driver session, or nothing when no session is running.

This keyword takes no parameters.

```csv
App Info,Get Driver Session Id
```

Good to know:

- The CSV and YAML runner discards the id. It's useful from Python, `optics serve` and MCP.

### Initialise Setup

Does nothing. It exists for compatibility and writes a debug log line only.

This keyword takes no parameters.

```csv
Setup,Initialise Setup
```

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/actions

# Action keywords

> Learn how to tap, type, swipe, scroll and send keys in a step.

Action keywords do something to the app: tap, type, swipe, scroll or press a key. Each one looks at the current screen once and fails if the element isn't there. They don't wait.

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2
Sign In,Assert Presence,${email_field},15
Sign In,Enter Text,${email_field},ana@birch.example
Sign In,Enter Text,${password_field},@:pw-ana
Sign In,Press Element,${sign_in}
```

Put an [Assert Presence](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/verification#assert-presence) before an action when the screen may still be loading. For how `element`, `index`, `${name}` and the `aoi_*` parameters work, see [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/).

**TV platforms:**
On Samsung Tizen and LG webOS TVs, keywords that tap, swipe, scroll or type fail with error E0105. Use [Press Keycode](#press-keycode) to move focus and select. Android TV works like Android. See [TV](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv).

Before each action, Optics saves a screenshot to the run's output folder. See [Results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).

## Tap

### Press Element

Taps or clicks an element found by XPath, text, OCR or image.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to tap. See [Element arguments](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#element-arguments). |
| `repeat` | `1` | How many times to tap. |
| `offset_x` | `0` | Pixels to add to the tap point horizontally. |
| `offset_y` | `0` | Pixels to add to the tap point vertically. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to tap when several match. `0` is the first. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. See [Area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest). |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. See [Event names](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#event-names). |

```csv
Sign In,Press Element,${sign_in}
Browse,Press Element,Trail Runner 2,index=1
Checkout,Press Element,pay_button.png,aoi_y=50,aoi_height=50
Add To Cart,Press Element,${add_to_cart},event_name=tap_add_to_cart
```

```yaml
- Press Element ${sign_in} event_name=tap_sign_in
```

Good to know:

- Press Element doesn't wait. If the element isn't on screen yet, the step fails.
- `repeat` taps several times only when the element was found in the app's UI tree, by XPath or native text. An element found by OCR or image is tapped once.
- `offset_x` and `offset_y` apply only when the element was found by OCR or image. They're ignored for elements found in the UI tree.
- When `element` is `${name}` with several values, Optics tries each one until it finds the element.
- If [self-healing](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal) is turned on, it gets one try to recover before the step fails.
- When a locator matches several elements, the log says how many matched and which one Optics used. Set `index` or use a more specific locator to pick another.

### Press By Percentage

Taps a point given as a percentage of the screen width and height.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `percent_x` | Required | Horizontal position, from 0 (left) to 100 (right). |
| `percent_y` | Required | Vertical position, from 0 (top) to 100 (bottom). |
| `repeat` | `1` | How many times to tap. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Promo,Press By Percentage,50,90
Promo,Press By Percentage,50,90,event_name=tap_banner
```

```yaml
- Press By Percentage 50 90
```

Good to know:

- Values are 0–100, not 0–1. `0.5` means half a percent, which taps the edge of the screen.
- On Appium, decimals are cut off: `50.7` taps at 50 %.
- We recommend Press Element instead. A fixed point breaks when the layout changes.

### Press By Coordinates

Taps an absolute pixel coordinate on the screen.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `coor_x` | Required | Horizontal position in pixels. |
| `coor_y` | Required | Vertical position in pixels. |
| `repeat` | `1` | Ignored. The point is always tapped once. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Promo,Press By Coordinates,540,1600
```

```yaml
- Press By Coordinates 540 1600
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, a failed tap is logged and the step passes. Follow it with an assertion to confirm the tap worked.
- On Selenium, Optics clicks whatever element is at that point of the page.
- To set `event_name`, write it by name: `Press By Coordinates,540,1600,event_name=tap_promo`.

### Detect And Press

Taps an element if it appears within the timeout. If it doesn't appear, the step passes without tapping.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to tap. |
| `timeout` | `30` | Seconds to wait for the element. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Open Birch,Detect And Press,Allow,5
Open Birch,Detect And Press,${newsletter_close},5
```

```yaml
- Detect And Press Allow 5
```

Good to know:

- Use it for pop-ups that appear only sometimes, such as permission prompts or a newsletter sign-up.
- Keep the timeout short. When the element never appears, the step waits the full timeout.
- In Python the default timeout is 10 seconds.

### Select Dropdown Option

Opens a dropdown and picks an option, scrolling inside the list if the option isn't visible.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The dropdown to open. |
| `option` | Required | The option to pick: text, an XPath or an image file name. |
| `timeout` | `30` | Seconds to keep scrolling the list before failing. Decimals are allowed. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Product,Select Dropdown Option,${size_dropdown},US 9,20
```

```yaml
- Select Dropdown Option ${size_dropdown} "US 9" 20
```

Good to know:

- Optics taps the dropdown and picks the option if it's visible. Otherwise it finds the list that opened and scrolls it down half a list at a time, until the option appears or the list stops moving.
- It assumes the list opens with its first option visible.
- If the option isn't found, the error lists the options Optics did see.

## Type

### Enter Text

Types text into a field.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The field to type into. |
| `text` | Required | The text to type, or one special key such as `<enter>`. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to use when several match. |

```csv
Search,Enter Text,${search_bar},Trail Runner 2
Search,Enter Text,${search_bar},<enter>
Sign In,Enter Text,${password_field},@:pw-ana
```

```yaml
- Enter Text ${search_bar} "Trail Runner 2"
```

Good to know:

- Enter Text doesn't clear the field first. Use [Clear Element Text](#clear-element-text) before it if the field may have text.
- `event_name` comes before `index` here, unlike Press Element. Set `index` by name: `index=1`.
- When the field was found by OCR or image, Optics taps it, then types.
- A value that is exactly one special key in angle brackets presses that key. Appium supports `<enter>`, `<tab>`, `<backspace>`, `<space>`, `<escape>`, `<back>`, `<home>`, `<menu>`, `<volumeup>`, `<volumedown>`, `<power>`, `<camera>` and `<search>`. Selenium supports `<enter>`, `<tab>`, `<backspace>`, `<space>` and `<escape>`. An unknown name is typed literally.
- Start a value with `@:` to mark it as sensitive. Optics masks it as `****` in log files and removes the `@:` before typing.
- `element` can be the caption next to a field, such as `Mobile Number`. When only one field fits the caption, Optics types into that field. This works on the web, Android and iOS.
- In YAML, quote text that contains spaces.

### Enter Number

Types a number into a field. It works like Enter Text without special keys.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The field to type into. |
| `number` | Required | The number to type. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to use when several match. |

```csv
Cart,Enter Number,${quantity_field},2
```

```yaml
- Enter Number ${quantity_field} 2
```

### Enter Text Direct

Types text into whichever field has focus, without looking for an element.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | Required | The text to type. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Search,Press Element,${search_bar}
Search,Enter Text Direct,pace knit
```

```yaml
- Enter Text Direct "pace knit"
```

Good to know:

- Special keys such as `<enter>` aren't recognized here. They're typed as text. Use Enter Text Using Keyboard for keys.
- It types at once, into whatever has focus. To type into a known field, use Enter Text with its locator. On the web, Enter Text waits until the field accepts input.

### Enter Text Using Keyboard

Types text one key at a time, or presses one special key.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `text_input` | Required | The text to type, or one special key such as `<enter>`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Search,Enter Text Using Keyboard,<enter>
Search,Enter Text Using Keyboard,trail runner
```

```yaml
- Enter Text Using Keyboard <enter>
```

Good to know:

- Write special keys in angle brackets. `enter` without brackets types the word "enter".
- Use it for apps that ignore text sent all at once, such as search fields that react to each key press.

### Clear Element Text

Empties a text field.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The field to clear. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to use when several match. |

```csv
Search,Clear Element Text,${search_bar}
```

```yaml
- Clear Element Text ${search_bar}
```

Good to know:

- When the field was found by OCR or image, Optics taps it and clears it. On Playwright it selects all and deletes.
- `element` can be the caption next to the field, the same as for Enter Text.

## Swipe and scroll

Directions don't all mean the same thing. For the swipe keywords and Scroll From Element on Appium, the direction is the way your finger moves: `up` reveals content further down. Scroll, Scroll Until Element Appears and every Playwright gesture use the page's direction instead: `down` reveals content further down.

### Swipe

Swipes from a pixel point in a direction.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `coor_x` | Required | Start point, horizontal pixels. |
| `coor_y` | Required | Start point, vertical pixels. |
| `direction` | `right` | `up`, `down`, `left` or `right`. |
| `swipe_length` | `50` | Distance to move, in pixels. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Browse,Swipe,540,1500,up,800
```

```yaml
- Swipe 540 1500 up 800
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, an unknown direction or a driver error is logged and the step passes.
- Selenium doesn't support Swipe. The step fails.
- On Playwright, Swipe scrolls the page with the mouse wheel by `swipe_length` pixels. `down` scrolls down, and every other direction scrolls up.

### Swipe By Percentage

Swipes from a point given in percent, for a distance given in percent of the screen.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `percent_x` | Required | Start point, 0–100 of the screen width. Whole numbers only. |
| `percent_y` | Required | Start point, 0–100 of the screen height. Whole numbers only. |
| `direction` | `right` | `up`, `down`, `left` or `right`. |
| `swipe_length` | `50` | Distance, in percent of the screen height for `up` and `down`, or width for `left` and `right`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Browse,Swipe By Percentage,50,80,up,40
Banner,Swipe By Percentage,90,30,left,60
```

```yaml
- Swipe By Percentage 50 80 up 40
```

Good to know:

- Decimals such as `50.5` fail the step.
- Selenium doesn't support it. On Playwright it scrolls the page vertically by `swipe_length` percent of the window height.

### Swipe From Element

Swipes starting on an element, such as a carousel or slider.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to start on. |
| `direction` | Required | `up`, `down`, `left` or `right`. |
| `swipe_length` | Required | Distance to move, in pixels. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to use when several match. |

```csv
Product,Swipe From Element,${product_carousel},left,300
```

```yaml
- Swipe From Element ${product_carousel} left 300
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, driver errors during the gesture are logged and the step passes.
- Selenium doesn't support it. On Playwright, it scrolls the element's nearest scrollable area.
- In Python, `direction` defaults to `right` and `swipe_length` to `50`.

### Swipe Until Element Appears

Swipes again and again until an element is on screen.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to look for. |
| `direction` | Required | `up`, `down`, `left` or `right`. |
| `timeout` | Required | Seconds to keep trying. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Browse,Swipe Until Element Appears,Pace Knit,up,30
```

```yaml
- Swipe Until Element Appears "Pace Knit" up 30
```

Good to know:

- Each round checks for the element for up to 3 seconds, swipes a quarter of the screen starting near the left edge at mid-height, then waits 3 seconds.
- Selenium doesn't support it. On Playwright, use `down` to move down the page.
- In Python, `direction` defaults to `down` and `timeout` to `30`.

### Scroll

Scrolls the screen once.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | Required | `down` to reveal content below, `up` to reveal content above. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Browse,Scroll,down
```

```yaml
- Scroll down
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, only `up` and `down` work. `left` and `right` do nothing and the step passes.
- On Appium, one scroll drags from 80 % to 20 % of the screen height.
- On Selenium, one scroll moves one window's height or width, in any of the four directions.
- On Playwright, one scroll moves about 240 pixels.
- In Python, `direction` defaults to `down`.

### Scroll From Element

Scrolls starting on an element, such as a list inside a page. It behaves the same as Swipe From Element.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to start on. |
| `direction` | Required | `up`, `down`, `left` or `right`. |
| `scroll_length` | Required | Distance to move, in pixels. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to use when several match. |

```csv
Browse,Scroll From Element,${product_list},up,600
```

```yaml
- Scroll From Element ${product_list} up 600
```

Good to know:

- On Appium the direction is the way your finger moves, as with Swipe From Element.
- In Python, `direction` defaults to `down` and `scroll_length` to `100`.

### Scroll Until Element Appears

Scrolls again and again until an element is on screen.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to look for. |
| `direction` | Required | `down` or `up`. |
| `timeout` | Required | Seconds to keep trying. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Browse,Scroll Until Element Appears,Pace Knit,down,40
```

```yaml
- Scroll Until Element Appears "Pace Knit" down 40
```

Good to know:

- Each round checks for the element for up to 3 seconds, scrolls once, then waits 3 seconds.
- If the element never appears, the step fails with error E0201.
- In Python, `direction` defaults to `down` and `timeout` to `30`.

## Keys and scripts

### Press Keycode

Sends a hardware, system or remote-control key.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `keycode` | Required | The key to send. Its form depends on the platform. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

| Platform | What to pass | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Android | An Android keycode number | `4` Back, `3` Home, `66` Enter |
| Samsung Tizen and LG webOS TV | A remote key name | `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `ENTER`, `BACK`, `HOME`, `PLAY`, `PAUSE` |
| Playwright | A key name | `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `ArrowUp` |

```csv
Product,Press Keycode,4
TV Browse,Press Keycode,RIGHT
TV Browse,Press Keycode,ENTER
```

```yaml
- Press Keycode 4
```

Good to know:

- Selenium doesn't support it. Use Enter Text with `<enter>` or `<tab>` instead.
- On TVs, this is how you move focus and select. See [TV](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv).

### Execute Script

Runs a driver command, such as an Appium `mobile:` command, or JavaScript in the browser.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `script_or_json` | Required | The script, or JSON with `script` and `args` keys. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Device,Execute Script,"{""script"": ""mobile: pressKey"", ""args"": {""keycode"": 3}}"
Web,Execute Script,"window.scrollTo(0, 0)"
```

```yaml
- Execute Script '{"script":"mobile: pressKey","args":{"keycode":3}}'
```

Good to know:

- In CSV, wrap a value that contains commas in double quotes, and double every quote inside it.
- When the value is JSON with a `script` key, `args` is passed this way: an object becomes one argument, and a list becomes one argument per item.
- The CSV and YAML runner can't store the result. It's returned over `optics serve`, MCP and [Python](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/python).
- The BLE driver doesn't support it.

## Read and wait

### Get Text

Reads the text of an element. For a text field on the web, it reads what the field holds.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to read. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to read when several match. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |

```csv
Product,Get Text,//android.widget.TextView[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/price"]
```

```yaml
- Get Text //android.widget.TextView[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/price"]
```

Good to know:

- Add `store_as=name` to keep the text for later steps as `${name}`. See [Keep what a keyword returns](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/variables#keep-what-a-keyword-returns).
- To fail the step when the text is wrong, use [Assert Text](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/verification#assert-text).
- When the element is found only by OCR or image, Get Text returns nothing and the step still passes.
- In Python, Get Text takes `element` only and returns the text.

### Sleep

Waits a number of seconds.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `duration` | Required | Seconds to wait. Whole numbers only. |

```csv
Checkout,Sleep,3
```

```yaml
- Sleep 3
```

Good to know:

- `1.5` fails the step. Use `1` or `2`.
- We recommend an assertion with a timeout instead. It continues as soon as the element appears.

## Deprecated

These keywords still run but will be removed. Use the replacement shown.

### Press Checkbox

Taps an element and logs a deprecation warning. Use [Press Element](#press-element) instead.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The checkbox to tap. |
| `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width`, `aoi_height` | `0`, `0`, `100`, `100` | Area of the screen to search, in percent. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `index` | `0` | Which match to tap when several match. |

```csv
Checkout,Press Checkbox,${terms_checkbox}
```

### Press Radio Button

Taps an element and logs a deprecation warning. Use [Press Element](#press-element) instead. It takes the same parameters as Press Checkbox.

```csv
Checkout,Press Radio Button,${express_shipping}
```

### Swipe Seekbar To Right Android

Meant to drag a slider to the right. It fails on Appium. Use [Swipe From Element](#swipe-from-element) instead.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The slider. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Filters,Swipe From Element,${price_slider},right,300
```

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/verification

# Verification keywords

> Learn which keyword to use for each check, and how long each one waits.

Verification keywords check what's on screen. Assertions wait up to a timeout for an element, so they're also how you wait for a screen to load before an action.

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3
Sign In,Press Element,${sign_in}
Sign In,Assert Presence,Welcome|Trail Runner 2,20,any
```

We recommend Assert Presence for most checks. Use Assert Visibility when the element must be on screen right now, not only in the page. For how `element` values are read, see [Element arguments](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#element-arguments).

## Check several elements at once

Assert Presence, Assert Visibility, Validate Element and Validate Screen accept several elements separated by `|` (a pipe). `rule` decides whether `any` or `all` of them must be found.

```csv
Home,Assert Presence,Welcome|Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit,20,all
```

**Common mistake:**
Separate elements with `|`, never commas. Don't put spaces around the pipe. In a pipe list, `${a}|${b}` uses the first value of each variable. To try each value of a variable, store the whole `Welcome|Trail Runner 2` as one value and pass `${home_markers}`.

## Assertions

### Assert Presence

Fails unless the elements exist in the app within the timeout.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `elements` | Required | One element, or several separated by `\|`. |
| `timeout_str` | `30` | Seconds to wait. |
| `rule` | `any` | `any` passes when one element is found. `all` needs every element. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. See [Event names](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#event-names). |
| `fail` | `true` | Has almost no effect. A missing element fails the step even when it's `false`. |

```csv
Sign In,Assert Presence,Welcome
Sign In,Assert Presence,Welcome,20
Sign In,Assert Presence,${account_badge},timeout_str=20
Home,Assert Presence,Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit,20,all
```

```yaml
- Assert Presence Welcome 20
- Assert Presence Welcome timeout_str=20
```

Good to know:

- The timeout parameter is called `timeout_str`, not `timeout`. `timeout=20` is passed as the text "timeout=20" and fails the step. Write `20` positionally or `timeout_str=20`.
- "Present" means the element is in the app's UI tree, even if it's scrolled off screen. On Android, the UI tree usually leaves out off-screen items. To include them, set `appium:settings: {allowInvisibleElements: true}` in your [config](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config).
- Elements are checked in groups: text first, then XPaths, then images. Each group gets the full timeout. With `rule=any`, a text group that isn't found fails the step before the XPaths are tried. Keep one kind of locator per assertion when you use `any`.
- CSS selectors, `id:` locators and class names are skipped. If every element is one of those, the step passes without checking anything. Use text or an XPath.
- In Python the parameter is `timeout`, its default is 60 seconds, and there's no `fail` parameter.

### Assert Visibility

Fails unless the elements are on screen within the timeout. It takes the same parameters as Assert Presence.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `elements` | Required | One element, or several separated by `\|`. |
| `timeout_str` | `30` | Seconds to wait. |
| `rule` | `any` | `any` or `all`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |
| `fail` | `true` | Has almost no effect, as with Assert Presence. |

```csv
Home,Assert Visibility,${promo_banner},10
```

```yaml
- Assert Visibility ${promo_banner} 10
```

Good to know:

- On Appium, Optics checks that the element is rendered on screen. On Selenium and Playwright, only OCR and image matching can check visibility, so you need [text or image detection](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/text-and-images) configured. Without it, the step fails with "No strategies found".
- OCR and image matches always count as visible, because they come from a screenshot.
- The same grouping and CSS caveats as Assert Presence apply.

### Validate Element

Fails unless an element exists within the timeout. It's Assert Presence with a shorter default timeout and `all` as the default rule.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | One element, or several separated by `\|`. |
| `timeout` | `10` | Seconds to wait. |
| `rule` | `all` | `any` or `all`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Home,Validate Element,${search_bar},15
```

```yaml
- Validate Element ${search_bar} 15
```

Good to know:

- When `element` is `${name}` with several values, Optics tries each one until it finds the element.

### Validate Screen

Checks whether elements are present, without failing the step.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `elements` | Required | One element, or several separated by `\|`. |
| `timeout` | `30` | Seconds to wait. |
| `rule` | `any` | `any` or `all`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Home,Validate Screen,Welcome|Trail Runner 2,10
```

```yaml
- Validate Screen Welcome|Trail Runner 2 10
```

Good to know:

- Validate Screen never fails a step. In a CSV or YAML suite it only waits and logs the result. Use Assert Presence when the check must fail the test.
- From Python, `optics serve` and MCP it returns true or false.

### Is Element

Checks that an element is visible, invisible, enabled, disabled, checked or unchecked.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to check. |
| `element_state` | Required | `visible`, `invisible`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `checked` or `unchecked`. |
| `timeout` | Required | Seconds to wait. Used for `visible` and `invisible` only. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Checkout,Is Element,${place_order},enabled,5
Checkout,Is Element,${loading_spinner},invisible,15
Checkout,Is Element,${accept_terms},checked,5
```

```yaml
- Is Element ${place_order} enabled 5
```

Good to know:

- `visible` checks presence in the UI tree, the same way Assert Presence does.
- `invisible` doesn't wait for an element to go away. If the element is there, the step fails at once. If it isn't, the step waits the full timeout, then passes.
- `enabled`, `disabled`, `checked` and `unchecked` need an element found in the UI tree, by XPath or native text. An element found only by OCR or image fails the step.
- `checked` and `unchecked` work for checkboxes, radio buttons and switches.
- On the web, `aria-disabled="true"` counts as disabled, and `aria-checked` counts as checked.
- You must give a timeout, even for `enabled`, `disabled`, `checked` and `unchecked`.

### Assert Equality

Compares two values as text, after trimming spaces. It never fails the step.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `output` | Required | The first value. Can be `${name}`. |
| `expression` | Required | The second value. Can be `${name}`. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event, recorded only when the values match. |

```csv
Cart,Evaluate,total,${price} * 2
Cart,Assert Equality,${total},240
```

```yaml
- Assert Equality ${total} 240
```

Good to know:

- A mismatch returns false but doesn't fail the test. To fail on a wrong value on screen, use [Assert Text](#assert-text).
- Nothing is evaluated. `2+2` and `4` don't match, and quotes are compared as characters.
- When `${name}` has several values, only the first is used.

### Assert Text

Checks that an element shows the text you expect, and fails the step if it doesn't. For a text field, it checks what the field holds.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | Required | The element to read, by XPath, CSS or text. |
| `expected` | Required | The text to expect. Can be `${name}`. |
| `timeout` | `10` | Seconds to wait for the text. |
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Cart,Assert Text,${cart_total},$128.00
Profile,Assert Text,${email_field},${email},5
```

```yaml
- Assert Text ${cart_total} $128.00
```

Good to know:

- Spaces at the start and end are ignored on both sides.
- The element must be in the UI tree, found by XPath, CSS or native text. An element found only by OCR or image fails the step at once.
- If the element isn't found, the step fails with element not found, and Optics tries the next value of a `${name}` element.
- If the text is still wrong at the timeout, the error shows the text the element had.
- Start `expected` with `@:` to check a secret, such as a PIN. Optics compares it without the prefix and shows `****` in the error.

## Capture and inspect

These keywords save what's on screen to the run's output folder. See [Results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results). The return value reaches you over `optics serve`, MCP and [Python](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/python).

### Capture Screenshot

Takes a screenshot.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Checkout,Capture Screenshot
```

```yaml
- Capture Screenshot
```

Good to know:

- The image is saved only when `save_captures` is `true` in your [config](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config). It's on by default.
- The step fails with error E0303 if the screenshot fails or is completely black.

### Capture Pagesource

Saves the current UI tree as XML (apps) or HTML (web).

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | Empty | Label for a timed event. |

```csv
Checkout,Capture Pagesource
```

```yaml
- Capture Pagesource
```

Good to know:

- Use it to find XPaths for your elements file. See [Define elements](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/define).
- The step fails if no page source is available.

### Get Interactive Elements

Lists the elements on screen that you can tap or type into, and saves the list as a JSON file.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `filter_config` | Empty | Which elements to list: `all`, `interactive`, `buttons`, `inputs`, `images` or `text`. Empty lists all. |
| `compact` | `false` | `true` returns a short form of each element: label, class, bounds and actions. |

```csv
Debug,Get Interactive Elements,buttons
```

```yaml
- Get Interactive Elements buttons compact=true
```

### Get Screen Elements

Takes a screenshot and lists every element on screen in one step.

This keyword takes no parameters.

```csv
Debug,Get Screen Elements
```

```yaml
- Get Screen Elements
```

Good to know:

- Element positions are given in screenshot pixels, so they line up with the image.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow

# Flow control keywords

> Learn how to reuse modules, loop, branch, load data, compute values and call APIs in a suite.

Flow control keywords run other modules, repeat them, choose between them, and create variables you can use in later steps.

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3
Checkout Flow,Execute Module,Sign In
Checkout Flow,Run Loop,Add Product,product,Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit
Checkout Flow,Condition,${coupon} == 'none',Pay Full Price,Apply Coupon
```

## Rules for every flow keyword

- **Targets are module names.** Execute Module, Run Loop and Condition run modules, not single keywords. Multi-word names are fine in CSV. In YAML, quote them: `"Add Product"`.
- **Write the variable you create as a bare name.** Read Data, Evaluate, Date Evaluate and Run Loop take the name of a variable to write. Write `total`, not `${total}`. A `${total}` cell is replaced before the keyword runs, so the step fails if `total` doesn't exist yet. The log shows a harmless warning about the bare name.
- **Values are text.** Every variable holds text. Compare with quoted literals: `${status} == 'ready'`, `${count} == '3'`. A numeric comparison such as `${count} > 3` fails in Condition. See [Compare numbers](#compare-numbers) for the workaround.
- **Lists use pipes.** Separate values with `|`: `Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit`.
- **Steps inside a target are stricter.** In a module run by Execute Module, Run Loop or Condition, write every parameter positionally, because `name=value` isn't recognized there. `${name}` uses only the first value, with no fallback to the next one. Any error inside is reported as error E0401.

Flow control keywords aren't available as MCP tools. They work in CSV and YAML suites, `optics live`, `optics serve` and [Python](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/python).

## Reuse and repeat

### Execute Module

Runs another module's steps from inside a module.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `module_name` | Required | The module to run. |

```csv
Checkout Flow,Execute Module,Sign In
Checkout Flow,Execute Module,Add To Cart
```

```yaml
- Execute Module "Sign In"
```

Good to know:

- Use Execute Module whenever one module calls another. A row whose keyword cell is a module name fails with "Keyword not found".
- A module can't run itself.
- Python doesn't have Execute Module. Call your own Python functions instead.

### Run Loop

Runs a module a number of times, or once for each value in one or more lists.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | Required | The module to run. |
| then one of: | | |
| `count` | | A whole number of times to run, 1 or more. |
| `variable`, `values`, … | | Pairs of a variable name and its list of values. Add as many pairs as you need. |

`values` can be:

- a pipe-separated list: `Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit`. Spaces around each value are trimmed.
- a JSON list: `["Trail Runner 2", "Pace Knit"]`.
- `${name}`, where the element `name` holds either of the above.

```csv
Fill Cart,Run Loop,Add Trail Runner,3
Fill Cart,Run Loop,Add Product,product,Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit
Fill Cart,Run Loop,Add Product,product,${featured},size,US 9|US 10
```

```yaml
- Run Loop "Add Product" product "Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit"
```

Inside the target module, use `${product}` to read the current value:

```csv
Add Product,Enter Text,${search_bar},${product}
Add Product,Enter Text,${search_bar},<enter>
Add Product,Assert Presence,${add_to_cart},10
Add Product,Press Element,${add_to_cart}
```

Good to know:

- With several lists, the loop runs as many times as the shortest list.
- The variable keeps its last value after the loop ends.
- A list stored in an elements file needs CSV quoting if it's JSON: `featured,"[""Trail Runner 2"",""Pace Knit""]"`. A pipe list needs none: `featured,Trail Runner 2|Pace Knit`.
- An odd number of parameters after the target, other than a single count, fails with error E0403.

## Branch

### Condition

Runs a module only when a condition is true, like if, else-if and else.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `condition`, `target`, … | Required | Pairs of a condition and the module to run when it's true. Add as many pairs as you need. |
| `else_target` | Empty | A module to run when no condition is true. Give it as the last parameter. |

The conditions are checked in order. The first true one runs its target, and the rest are skipped. With an odd number of parameters, the last one is the else target.

A condition is one of two kinds:

- **A module name.** Optics runs that module. If every step passes, the condition is true. Start the name with `!` to flip it: `!Is Signed In` is true when the module fails.
- **An expression.** Each `${name}` is replaced with its value in double quotes, so compare it with a quoted literal. You can use `==`, `!=`, `and`, `or` and `not`. Start the expression with `!` to negate it.

```csv
Start,Condition,Is Signed In,Go Home,Sign In
Start,Condition,!Is Signed In,Sign In
Pay,Condition,${payment} == 'card',Pay By Card,${payment} == 'wallet',Pay By Wallet,Pay On Delivery
```

```yaml
- Condition ${payment}=='card' "Pay By Card" "Pay On Delivery"
```

Good to know:

- A module condition really runs its steps. Use one that only checks, such as a module with a single Assert Presence.
- If no condition is true and there's no else target, the step passes and nothing runs.
- If the target module fails, the step fails.
- In YAML, write the expression without spaces: `${payment}=='card'`. A quoted expression that contains `=` keeps its quotes and fails.

### Compare numbers

Condition compares text, so `${count} > 3` fails. Compute the comparison with [Evaluate](#evaluate) first, which does arithmetic, then test its `True` or `False` result:

```csv
Shipping,Evaluate,free_shipping,${item_count} > 3
Shipping,Condition,${free_shipping} == 'True',Expect Free Shipping,Expect Paid Shipping
```

## Create variables

### Read Data

Loads a value from a CSV or JSON file, or an environment variable, into a variable.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `input_element` | Required | The variable to write. Write a bare name. |
| `file_path` | Required | A `.csv` or `.json` file, or `ENV:NAME` for an environment variable. Relative paths start at the project folder. |
| `query` | Empty | Which rows and columns to keep. See below. |

The query has parts separated by `;`:

- `select=column` keeps one column. `select=a,b` keeps several.
- A filter such as `tier == 'gold'` keeps the matching rows. Several filters must all match.
- `${name}` inside the query is replaced with its value in single quotes, so write `email == ${email}`.

Given this data file:

`test_data/users.csv`:

```csv
email,password,tier
ana@birch.example,pw-ana,gold
ben@birch.example,pw-ben,basic
```

```csv
Load User,Read Data,gold_email,test_data/users.csv,tier == 'gold';select=email
Load User,Read Data,ana_tier,test_data/users.csv,email == 'ana@birch.example';select=tier
Load Token,Read Data,api_token,ENV:BIRCH_API_TOKEN
```

```yaml
- Read Data gold_email test_data/users.csv tier=='gold';select=email
```

After these steps, `${gold_email}` is `ana@birch.example` and `${ana_tier}` is `gold`.

Good to know:

- Every cell is read as text, so filters must compare text: `age == '30'`. `age > 26` fails with error E0403.
- Narrow the result to one row and one column. One row with several columns is stored joined by commas, such as `ana@birch.example,gold`. Several rows are stored in a form you can't use in a step.
- A query that matches nothing fails with "No data found". A missing column fails with error E0403. A missing file or environment variable fails with error E0501.
- **JSON files** can be a list of objects, one per row. If the top level is an object, Optics uses its first list. Nested keys become dotted column names, such as `address.city`.
- **Environment variables** are stored as they are, such as `ENV:BIRCH_API_TOKEN` giving `abc123`. A value that starts with `{` or `[` is read as JSON, and one with several lines is read as CSV.
- In CSV, wrap a query that contains commas in double quotes: `"tier == 'gold';select=email,password"`.
- In YAML, write filters without spaces.

### Evaluate

Computes an expression and saves the result in a variable.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `param1` | Required | The variable to write. Write a bare name. |
| `param2` | Required | The expression to compute. |

```csv
Cart,Evaluate,total,${price} * 2
Cart,Evaluate,label,'free' if ${total} > 100 else 'paid'
Cart,Evaluate,greeting,'Hello ' + '${first_name}'
```

```yaml
- Evaluate total "${price} * 2"
```

Good to know:

- Each `${name}` is replaced with its value as written, without quotes. Numbers work as numbers. Put quotes around text values: `'${first_name}'`.
- You can use numbers, quoted text, lists, `+ - * / % **`, comparisons, `and`, `or`, `not` and `x if condition else y`.
- Function calls such as `int(...)` or `len(...)` aren't allowed. They fail with "Unsafe expression".
- The result is saved as text. A comparison saves `True` or `False`.
- In CSV, wrap an expression that contains commas in double quotes.

### Date Evaluate

Adds or subtracts days from a date and saves the result, formatted the way you choose.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `param1` | Required | The variable to write. Write a bare name. |
| `param2` | Required | The start date. |
| `param3` | Required | `+N days`, `-N days`, `today` or `now`. |
| `param4` | `%d %B` | The output format, such as `%Y-%m-%d`. |

The start date can be in any of these forms. They're tried in this order:

| Format | Example |
|---|---|
| Month/day/year | `10/24/2026` |
| Day/month/year | `24/10/2026` |
| Year-month-day | `2026-10-24` |
| Day-month-year | `24-10-2026` |
| Year/month/day | `2026/10/24` |

```csv
Delivery,Date Evaluate,delivery_date,${order_date},+5 days
Delivery,Assert Presence,${delivery_date},10
```

```yaml
- Date Evaluate delivery_date ${order_date} "+5 days" "%d %B"
```

With `order_date` set to `2026-10-10` in your elements file, `${delivery_date}` is `15 October`.

Good to know:

- Only days work. `+1 week` fails with error E0403. Put a space between the number and `days`.
- `today` and `now` don't read the clock. They keep the start date as it is, which is useful to reformat a date.
- An ambiguous date such as `03/04/2026` is read as March 4.
- Use a variable name that has no value yet, and don't add it to your elements file. If the name already has a value, Date Evaluate adds the new date after it, and `${name}` keeps giving the old value. For the same reason, don't reuse the name inside a loop.
- Common format codes are `%d` day, `%m` month number, `%B` month name, `%b` short month name and `%Y` year.

### Invoke API

Calls an HTTP API that you define in YAML and saves values from the response as variables.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `api_identifier` | Required | The API to call, as `collection.api`. |

Define your APIs in a YAML file anywhere in the project folder, with a top-level `api:` key. You can also put the `api:` block in your config.yaml.

`test_data/api.yaml`:

```yaml
api:
  collections:
    birch:
      name: "Birch API"
      base_url: "https://api.birch.example"
      global_headers:
        content-type: "application/json"
      apis:
        login:
          name: "Sign in"
          endpoint: "/v1/token"
          request:
            method: POST
            body:
              email: "${api_email}"
              password: "${api_password}"
          expected_result:
            jsonpath_assertions:
              - path: $.token
                condition: "len($) > 0"
            extract:
              auth_token: $.token
              customer_id: $.customer.id
        cart:
          name: "Get cart"
          endpoint: "/v1/customers/${customer_id}/cart"
          request:
            method: GET
            headers:
              Authorization: "Bearer ${auth_token}"
          expected_result:
            extract:
              cart_count: $.item_count
```

```csv
Prepare Cart,Invoke API,birch.login
Prepare Cart,Invoke API,birch.cart
```

```yaml
- Invoke API birch.login
```

After `birch.login`, `${auth_token}` and `${customer_id}` hold the extracted values.

Good to know:

- The URL is `base_url` plus `endpoint`. An absolute `endpoint` is used on its own.
- `${name}` is replaced anywhere in the endpoint, headers and body. A missing variable fails the step.
- The body is sent as JSON. Every request has a 30-second timeout.
- `extract` maps a variable name to a JSONPath. `$.a.b`, `a.b` and `[0]` indexing all work.
- Each `jsonpath_assertions` entry checks the value at `path`. In `condition`, `$` stands for that value, as in `len($) > 0` or `$ == 'ok'`. A false condition fails the step.
- `expected_status`, `json_schema` and `request.timeout` are accepted but not checked yet. Use a `jsonpath_assertions` entry to check the response instead.
- With `expected_result`, a response that isn't JSON fails the step with error E0403.
- Each call is logged to `api_details.log` and `api_details.har` in the run's output folder. See [Results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).
- The top-level key must be `api:`. A file that starts with `apis:` is ignored.

See [Call APIs from a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/api-calls) for a full walkthrough.

## Worked example: sign in as each user

This suite signs in as two Birch users, reads each user's tier from a data file, and checks for the gold badge only for gold users.

`test_cases/test_cases.csv`:

```csv
test_case,test_step
Sign In Every User,Open Birch
Sign In Every User,Sign In Everyone
```

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3,param_4,param_5
Open Birch,Launch App,com.birch.shop
Sign In Everyone,Run Loop,Sign In As,email,ana@birch.example|ben@birch.example,password,pw-ana|pw-ben
Sign In As,Assert Presence,${email_field},15
Sign In As,Enter Text,${email_field},${email}
Sign In As,Enter Text,${password_field},${password}
Sign In As,Press Element,${sign_in}
Sign In As,Assert Presence,Welcome,20
Sign In As,Read Data,tier,test_data/users.csv,email == ${email};select=tier
Sign In As,Condition,${tier} == 'gold',Check Gold Badge
Sign In As,Press Element,${sign_out}
Check Gold Badge,Assert Presence,Gold member,10
```

`test_data/elements.csv`:

```csv
Element_Name,Element_ID,Element_ID_text
email_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/email"],Email
password_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/password"],Password
sign_in,//android.widget.Button[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/sign_in"],Sign in
sign_out,//android.widget.Button[@resource-id="com.birch.shop:id/sign_out"],Sign out
```

`test_data/users.csv`:

```csv
email,password,tier
ana@birch.example,pw-ana,gold
ben@birch.example,pw-ben,basic
```

How it works:

- Run Loop runs `Sign In As` twice. It sets `email` and `password` to the next pair of values each time.
- Steps in `Sign In As` are positional, because it runs inside Run Loop. `Assert Presence,Welcome,20` is correct there. `timeout_str=20` wouldn't be.
- Read Data writes the bare name `tier`. Its query replaces `${email}` with the current email in quotes.
- Condition compares `${tier}` with the quoted literal `'gold'`. For Ben the condition is false, so nothing runs and the step passes.
- Inside the loop, `${email_field}` uses only its first value, the XPath. The `Email` fallback is used only by steps outside a loop.

- [Data-driven tests](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/data-driven)

- [Call APIs from a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/api-calls)
- [Organise tests](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/organise)

# CLI

> Look up every `optics` command, its flags, what it writes and the exit codes it returns.

The `optics` command creates projects, checks your setup, runs tests and starts the integration servers. This page covers Optics 1.10.5.

Commands are grouped by when you use them: getting started, running tests, integrating with other tools, and everything else. Run `optics <command> --help` to see the same flags in your terminal.

## Global behavior

```text
optics [--version] [--help] <command> [options]
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--version` | Prints `Optics Framework 1.10.5` and exits with code 0. |
| `--help`, `-h` | Lists the commands: `list`, `configure`, `config`, `doctor`, `quickstart`, `dry_run`, `init`, `execute`, `live`, `generate`, `setup`, `serve`, `mcp`, `completion`. |

There's no `optics version` command. Use `optics --version`.

When you run `optics` with no command for the first time, it prints a welcome panel that points to `optics quickstart`, `optics doctor` and `optics --help`. After that, it prints a one-line reminder. Optics remembers the first run in a small marker file under `~/.optics` (or `$OPTICS_HOME`).

If Optics can't load one of its own dependencies, every command stops with a red "Cannot start" panel. The panel shows the underlying error and the reinstall command for your environment, for example `pipx reinstall optics-framework` or `pip install --force-reinstall optics-framework`.

When a command fails unexpectedly, Optics prints `Unexpected error (<type>): <message>` and suggests running `optics doctor`. See [Exit codes](#exit-codes).

## `optics quickstart`

Walks you through creating your first project, installing an engine, writing config.yaml and running a test.

```text
optics quickstart
```

There are no flags. The command asks these questions in order:

1. **What do you want to automate?** `mobile` or `web`.
2. **Install the engine now?** Appium for mobile; Playwright and Selenium for web. If you decline, it prints the `optics setup --install` command to run later.
3. **Start from a sample?** The `contact` sample for mobile, the `playwright` sample for web. Decline to pick an empty project or another sample.
4. **Project name** (default `my-optics-project`) and **where it should live** (default: the current folder). If the folder exists, it asks for another name.
5. **Config questions.** If the sample ships its own config.yaml, you choose whether to overwrite it. The default is yes for mobile and no for web.
6. It runs `optics doctor` on the new project and shows the report.
7. If the report shows no blocking problems, it offers to run your first test with `optics execute`.

Quickstart never runs `optics dry_run`. It writes the same files as [`optics init`](#optics-init) and [`optics configure`](#optics-configure).

**Tip:**
The web path with the `playwright` sample needs no device or server. It's the fastest way to see a passing run.

## `optics init`

Creates a new project folder, either blank or copied from a sample.

```text
optics init [name] [--path DIR] [--template NAME] [--force] [--git-init]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Asks for it | The project name. The project goes in `<path>/<name>`. |
| `--path` | Current folder | The parent folder. Missing folders are created. |
| `--template` | Asks in a terminal; blank otherwise | Copies a sample project. One of `calendar`, `clock`, `contact`, `gmail_web`, `playwright`, `youtube`. |
| `--force` | Off | Deletes an existing folder with the same name first. Without it, an existing folder is an error and nothing is created. |
| `--git-init` | Off | Runs `git init` in the new project. Skipped quietly if Git isn't installed. |
| `--name` | | Deprecated. Pass the name as the first argument instead. |

In a terminal without `--template`, Optics shows a numbered list: `(Blank project)`, Contacts, Clock, Calendar, YouTube, Gmail Web and Playwright Web. Press Enter on a blank answer to cancel.

A blank project contains:

```tree
birch-tests/
├── config.yaml                 # commented starter config, every engine disabled
├── modules/modules.csv         # module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3
├── test_cases/test_cases.csv   # test_case,test_step
└── test_data/elements.csv      # Element_Name,Element_ID
```

| Sample | Target | Engines it uses |
|---|---|---|
| `contact` | Google Contacts on an Android emulator | Appium, EasyOCR. Includes an error definitions file. |
| `clock` | Android Clock app | Appium, Pytesseract, image templates. Shows `Run Loop`. |
| `calendar` | Android Calendar app | Appium, EasyOCR. Shows `Invoke API` and `Date Evaluate`. |
| `youtube` | YouTube on Android | Appium, EasyOCR, image templates. Shows `Condition`. |
| `gmail_web` | Gmail in Chrome | Selenium, EasyOCR. |
| `playwright` | `https://example.com` | Playwright. Needs no device or server. |

Example:

```shell
$ optics init birch-tests --template playwright --path ~/work --git-init
```

Exit code 3 if the project already exists, the template name is unknown, or the name is empty.

## `optics configure`

Writes a project's config.yaml by asking a few questions, or opens a full editor.

```text
optics configure [folder] [--edit]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Current folder | The project folder. It's created if it doesn't exist. |
| `--edit` | Off | Opens a full-screen editor over every config.yaml setting instead of the questions. |

**Guided mode** asks what you're automating (`android`, `ios`, `web-playwright` or `web-selenium`), then the details for that platform:

| Platform | Questions (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `android` | Device name (`emulator-5554`), platform name (`Android`), app package (`com.example.app`), main activity (`com.example.app.MainActivity`), Appium server URL (`http://127.0.0.1:4723`) |
| `ios` | Device or simulator name (`iPhone 15`), platform name (`iOS`), bundle identifier (`com.example.app`), Appium server URL |
| `web-selenium` | Selenium server URL (`http://127.0.0.1:4444/wd/hub`) |
| `web-playwright` | Browser (`chromium`), headless (no) |

Every platform then asks whether to find elements by on-screen text with EasyOCR, and the log level. If config.yaml already exists, Optics asks before overwriting it.

**Warning:**
The `web-selenium` answer writes `capabilities: {}`, which Selenium can't start with. Add `browserName: chrome` (or `firefox`) under `capabilities` before you run. See [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform).

**Editor mode** (`--edit`) uses these keys: ↑/↓ to move, Space to edit or toggle, S to save, Q to quit. Saving rewrites the whole file and removes your comments. Editing an engine list replaces it with `enabled: true` entries and drops their `url` and `capabilities`, so we recommend guided mode or a text editor for engine settings.

```shell
$ optics configure ./birch-tests
```

## `optics doctor`

Checks your Python, installed engines, device tools and project config, and tells you what to fix.

```text
optics doctor [folder] [--check]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | None | The project to validate. Without it, doctor checks your environment only and doesn't validate any config.yaml. |
| `--check` | Off | Exits with code 1 if any row is ❌. Use it in CI. |

Doctor prints one row per check: ✅ ok, ⚠️ warning (optional or not yet needed) or ❌ failure. Each problem row has a `→` hint with the fix.

| Section | What it checks |
|---|---|
| Core | Python version (Optics needs 3.12 or later), the installed Optics version, and whether this environment allows engine installs. |
| Engines | Whether each engine package is installed: Appium, BLE, Selenium, Playwright, EasyOCR, Pytesseract, Google Vision, Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic. |
| Mobile | `adb` on your PATH, connected Android devices, and whether the Appium server answers (the project's URL, or `127.0.0.1:4723`). |
| Web | The Playwright Chromium browser, and `chromedriver` or `geckodriver` on your PATH. |
| Project | With a folder: config.yaml parses, exactly one driver is enabled, the driver's element sources are enabled, and the driver has the settings it needs (for example `url`, `platformName`, and `bundleId` on iOS). |

Only project rows can be ❌. Environment rows are ✅ or ⚠️. Without `--check`, doctor always exits with 0.

Doctor doesn't check Selenium `capabilities`, and it doesn't create any output folders.

```shell
$ optics doctor ./birch-tests --check
```

## `optics setup`

Installs the optional engines Optics needs for your platform: drivers, OCR and LLM.

```text
optics setup [--install NAME [NAME ...]] [--list]
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| (none) | Opens a full-screen picker with checkboxes for each engine. |
| `--list` | Prints every engine and bundle you can install. Wins if you also pass `--install`. |
| `--install` | Installs the named engines or bundles. |

Names are case-insensitive. You can use an engine name (`appium`, `ble`, `selenium`, `playwright`, `easyocr`, `pytesseract`, `google-vision`, `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic`), a display name (`Gemini`, `Google Vision`) or a bundle (`mobile`, `web`, `vision`, `llm`, `all`). Pin a version with a standard specifier such as `appium==5.0.0` or `"easyocr>=1.7,<2.0"`.

`optics setup` installs into the same Python environment as Optics. If you install Playwright, it also downloads the Chromium browser. Some environments refuse installs, for example Conda, pipx and uv tool. See [Engines and extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines#where-installs-are-refused).

The MCP server isn't an engine here. The install scripts include it; with pip, install it with `pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"`.

```shell
$ optics setup --install appium easyocr
$ optics setup --install web gemini
```

Exit code 1 if a name is unknown, a version specifier is malformed (`appium=5.0.0`), or the install fails.

## `optics dry_run`

Checks a project for mistakes without running any step on a device.

```text
optics dry_run <folder> [--runner NAME] [--use-printer | --no-use-printer]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Required | The project folder. It must exist. |
| `--runner` | `test_runner` | The runner. Leave the default. |
| `--use-printer` / `--no-use-printer` | Printer on | Shows or hides the live result tree. |

A dry run checks that:

- Each test step names a module (or a keyword).
- Each module step names a real keyword. A typo gets a suggestion: `Did you mean 'Press Element'?`
- Each whole-cell `${name}` is defined in your elements files.

It doesn't run any keyword or touch the device. It does load the engines in config.yaml, so the engine extras must be installed, a driver must be enabled, and its settings must be valid (for example non-empty Appium `capabilities`).

**Common mistake:**
Variables that a step creates while running, such as the target of `Evaluate` or `Read Data`, don't exist yet during a dry run. Declare them in elements.csv with a placeholder value, for example `order_total,placeholder`, so the dry run passes.

The output and exit codes are the same as [`optics execute`](#optics-execute). Dry runs write `junit_output.xml` to `execution_output/` but no screenshots.

## `optics execute`

Runs every test case in a project on the real device, browser or app, and records the results.

```text
optics execute <folder> [--runner NAME] [--use-printer | --no-use-printer]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Required | The project folder. It must exist. |
| `--runner` | `test_runner` | The runner. We recommend the default. `pytest` is also accepted, but it needs the `pytest-cov` package installed. |
| `--use-printer` / `--no-use-printer` | Printer on | Shows or hides the live result tree. Turn it off for plain CI logs. |

There are no flags to pick tests or tags. To run a subset, use `include` or `exclude` in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#include-and-exclude).

What happens, in order:

1. Optics walks the whole folder and finds your files by their content (see [Project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#how-optics-finds-your-files)). It stops if there's no test cases file or no modules file.
2. It loads the config and stops if no driver is enabled.
3. **Preflight.** It checks that the first enabled driver can be reached. For Appium it connects to the server URL and, on Android, checks that `adb` finds a device. For Selenium it connects to the server URL. Playwright is skipped. If the check fails, Optics shows a "Cannot start" panel with the command that fixes it. Set `OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1` to skip this check.
4. It runs Suite Setup, then each test case, then Suite Teardown. A failing test case doesn't stop the others.
5. It saves a final screenshot and page source, and runs [error detection](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/error-detection) if the project has an error definitions file.

The printer shows a live tree, then a summary:

```terminal
Test Suite
└── Shopper can add a backpack                                     |      1.88s |    PASS
    ├── Open the store                                             |      0.85s |    PASS
    │   └── Launch App (https://www.saucedemo.com)                 |      0.85s |    PASS
```

```terminal
Total Test Cases: 1 | Passed: 1 | Failed: 0
```

When a step fails, a "Failure details" box names the test, the step and the reason:

```terminal
Shopper can add a backpack → step 'Press Elemnt (//input[@id='login-button'])' — Keyword not found: Press Elemnt. Did you mean 'Press Element'? (run `optics list` to see all keywords)
```

Results go to `execution_output/` in the project: `junit_output.xml`, screenshots, and logs if you turn them on. See [Project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#outputs).

| Exit code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Every test case passed. |
| 1 | Any test case failed, required files are missing, no driver is enabled, the preflight failed, or the folder doesn't exist. |

On-screen errors found by error detection appear in `junit_output.xml` as a failing test case, but they don't change the exit code.

```shell
$ optics execute ./birch-tests
$ OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1 optics execute ./birch-tests --no-use-printer
```

## `optics live`

Opens an interactive session where you type keywords, see each result straight away, and save what worked as a test.

```text
optics live [folder]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Current folder | The project folder. It must contain a config.yaml. |

The config must enable exactly one driver and at least one element source. Without a config, `optics live` stops with an error; there are no built-in defaults. Live runs `launch_app` as soon as it starts.

Type a keyword with its parameters, for example `press_element ${sign_in}` or `enter_text ${email_field} "ana@birch.example"`. Each result appears as two lines:

```terminal
  ✓ press_element ${sign_in}
     0.31s  [XPath]
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/save <test_case> <module>` | Saves the steps you've run since the last save as a module and a test case in CSV. Names can't contain spaces. |
| `/device [id]` | Lists connected Android and iOS devices, or switches to one. Appium only. |
| `/elements` | Shows the named elements in the project. |
| `/screenshot` | Saves a screenshot to `screenshots/` in the project. |
| `/help` | Shows help. |
| `/quit`, `/exit` | Quits. Warns once if you have unsaved steps. |

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Completes keyword names. |
| `${` | Suggests element names. |
| Ctrl+K | Opens the keyword browser. |
| Ctrl+N | Switches to plain-English mode. Needs an enabled `llm_models` entry. |
| Ctrl+X | Stops a running plain-English instruction. |
| Ctrl+C | Quits. |

Live writes its log to `logs/optics_live_<time>.log` and its screenshots to `screenshots/session_<time>/` in the project. See [Record a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/record) for a full walkthrough.

## `optics serve`

Starts the HTTP API so any language or tool can drive a device through Optics.

```text
optics serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--workers N]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. |
| `--port` | `8000` | The port to listen on. |
| `--workers` | `1` | Server processes. Keep it at 1: sessions live in memory and aren't shared between processes. |

**Warning:**
The API has no authentication and accepts requests from any web origin. Keep the default `127.0.0.1` unless you're on a trusted network.

The server doesn't read config.yaml. Each session gets its settings from the request. Interactive API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`. See [HTTP API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api).

```shell
$ optics serve --port 8000
```

## `optics mcp`

Starts the MCP server, which lets an AI agent such as Claude or Cursor drive a device with Optics keywords.

```text
optics mcp [--transport stdio|http] [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio` for agents that start the server themselves; `http` to serve at `http://<host>:<port>/mcp`. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--port` | `8090` | The port to listen on. `http` only. |

It needs the `mcp` extra, which the install scripts include. With pip: `pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"`. The `all` bundle doesn't include it. Without the extra, the command exits with code 1 and prints the install command. See [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp).

## `optics generate`

Turns a CSV or YAML project into pytest or Robot Framework code.

```text
optics generate <folder> [--framework pytest|robot] [--output FILE]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Required | The project folder. |
| `--framework` | `pytest` | `pytest` or `robot`. |
| `--output` | `test_generated.py` or `test_generated.robot` | A file name, not a path. The file always goes in `<folder>/generated/Tests/`. |

It writes:

- `generated/Tests/<file>`: the generated tests.
- `generated/requirements.txt`: the packages the generated code needs.
- `generated/Tests/input_templates/`: a copy of `input_templates/` if that folder sits at the project root.

Generate has stricter needs than `optics execute`:

- The config file must be named exactly `config.yaml`.
- The project needs an elements file. Only the `Element_ID` column is used; fallback columns are ignored.
- Flow-control keywords (`Run Loop`, `Condition`, `Evaluate` and the rest) and a few others are skipped without a warning.
- Suite Setup and Suite Teardown become ordinary tests.

Exit code 3 if a required file is missing or two files define the same name. See [Generate code](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/generate).

```shell
$ optics generate ./birch-tests --framework robot --output smoke.robot
```

## `optics list`

Prints every keyword you can use, grouped by category.

```text
optics list
```

Names are printed in snake_case. In a module, write them in Title Case with spaces: `press_element` becomes `Press Element`. Matching ignores case and spaces, so both forms work.

```terminal
ActionKeyword:
  - clear_element_text
  - detect_and_press
  ...
AppManagement:
  - launch_app
  ...
```

For parameters and examples, see [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/).

## `optics completion`

Turns on tab completion for `optics` in bash or zsh.

```text
optics completion
```

It writes `~/.optics/optics_completion.sh` and `~/.optics/optics_completion.zsh`, then offers to add a `source` line to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`, based on `$SHELL`. Other shells aren't supported. Restart your shell, or run `source ~/.zshrc`, to use it. To remove it, delete the line from your shell profile.

## `optics config`

Deprecated. Use [`optics configure`](#optics-configure).

```text
optics config
```

It prints a deprecation notice, then runs guided `optics configure` on the current folder. There's no global config file any more: every setting lives in the project's config.yaml.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success. For `optics execute` and `optics dry_run`, every test case passed. |
| `1` | A test case failed, a check failed (`optics doctor --check`, preflight), a required file or setting is missing, or an unexpected error occurred. |
| `2` | The command line was invalid, for example an unknown flag or a missing argument. |
| `3` | The input was invalid, for example a project that already exists, an unknown template, or files `optics generate` needs. The message starts with `Error:`. |
| `130` | You pressed Ctrl+C. Optics prints `Operation cancelled by user.` |

## Environment variables

None of these override config.yaml. Settings for `optics execute`, `dry_run` and `live` come only from the project's config.yaml.

| Variable | Used by | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT` | `execute` | Set to `1` or `true` to skip the server and device check before a run. |
| `OPTICS_HOME` | `optics` | Folder for the first-run marker. Default `~/.optics`. |
| `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` | `serve`, `mcp` | Set to `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` to turn on AI self-heal for every session by default. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER` | `serve`, `mcp` | The LLM engine for self-heal: `gemini` (default), `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL` | `serve`, `mcp` | The model for self-heal. Gemini defaults to `gemini-2.5-flash`; `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS` | `mcp` | Set to `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` to expose the `press_by_coordinates` and `press_by_percentage` tools. |
| `OPTICS_EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S` | `execute`, `serve` | Seconds to wait for events to flush at the end of a run. Default `2.0`. Raise it if `junit_output.xml` is cut short on long runs. |
| `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` | `doctor`, Playwright | Where Playwright browsers are installed. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Gemini | API key for the Gemini Developer API. |
| `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | Gemini, Google Vision | Use Vertex AI and Google Cloud credentials instead of an API key. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `openai` engine | API key for OpenAI. Set `api_key_env` in config.yaml to read another variable. |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `openai` engine | The server to call when the entry has no `url`, such as OpenRouter or a local Ollama. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `anthropic` engine | API key for the Claude API. |

`Read Data` can also read any variable with `ENV:<NAME>`. See [Flow control keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow).

## Install scripts

The install scripts put Optics in its own virtual environment under `~/.optics` and add the `optics` command to your PATH. They don't change your system Python. Python 3.12 or later is the one prerequisite.

**macOS and Linux**

```shell
$ curl -fsSL https://optics-framework.org/install | sh
```

Pass options after `sh -s --`:

```shell
$ curl -fsSL https://optics-framework.org/install | sh -s -- --extra appium,easyocr
```

| Option | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--version X.Y.Z` | `OPTICS_VERSION` | Installs a specific release. |
| `--extra a,b` | | Also installs engine extras, for example `appium,llm`. The `mcp` extra is always installed. |
| `--dir PATH` | `OPTICS_INSTALL_DIR` | Installs somewhere other than `~/.optics`. |
| `--no-modify-path` | `OPTICS_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Leaves your shell profile alone. |
| `--dry-run` | | Prints what would happen and changes nothing. |
| `--uninstall` | | Removes Optics and the PATH line it added to your shell profile. Other files in the folder are kept. |
| `--help` | | Shows the options. |

On Windows under Git Bash, MSYS2 or Cygwin, the script stops and points you to the PowerShell installer. Inside WSL, use this script.
**Windows**

```powershell
PS> irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1 | iex
```

Piping into `iex` can't pass parameters, so set environment variables first:

```powershell
PS> $env:OPTICS_EXTRA = "appium,easyocr"
PS> irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1 | iex
```

| Parameter (downloaded script) | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `-Version X.Y.Z` | `OPTICS_VERSION` | Installs a specific release. |
| `-Extra a,b` | `OPTICS_EXTRA` | Also installs engine extras. The `mcp` extra is always installed. |
| `-Dir PATH` | `OPTICS_INSTALL_DIR` | Installs somewhere other than `~\.optics`. |
| `-NoModifyPath` | `OPTICS_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Leaves your PATH alone. |
| `-DryRun` | | Prints what would happen and changes nothing. |
| `-Uninstall` | | Removes Optics and its entry in your user PATH. Other files in the folder are kept. |

To pass parameters without downloading the script, run it as a script block:

```powershell
PS> & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1))) -Uninstall
```
**pip**

```shell
$ python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"
```

Install into a virtual environment you control. Add [extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines) in the brackets.

See [Install Optics](https://optics-framework.org/docs/get-started/install) for a step-by-step guide.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config

# config.yaml

> Every setting in a project's config.yaml.

A project's config.yaml tells Optics which driver to use, how to find elements, and where to write logs and results. Every setting lives in the project; there's no global config file and no environment variable that overrides it.

Run [`optics configure`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#optics-configure) to write a working file by answering a few questions, then edit it by hand with this page.

## How Optics finds the file

| Command | Which file it reads |
|---|---|
| `optics execute`, `optics dry_run` | Any YAML file in the project tree that has `driver_sources` and `elements_sources`. The file name doesn't matter. If there are several, the last one found wins. |
| `optics live` | The first YAML file in the project tree with any config key. |
