| `optics doctor`, `optics configure`, `optics generate` | Exactly `<folder>/config.yaml`. |
| `optics serve`, `optics mcp` | None. Settings come from each session request. |

We recommend one file named `config.yaml` at the project root, so every command reads the same settings.

Settings you leave out take their defaults. Optics ignores keys it doesn't know, so a typo such as `log_levle` is silently skipped.

**Warning:**
If config.yaml has a wrong value type, `optics execute` logs the problem, skips the file and runs with defaults. The run then stops with "No driver enabled". Run `optics doctor <folder>` to find the problem.

## Top-level keys

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver_sources` | All disabled | The driver that controls the device or browser. See [driver_sources](#driver-sources). |
| `elements_sources` | All disabled | Where Optics looks for elements: the driver's UI tree, its locators, or its screenshots. `element_sources` is accepted as an alias. |
| `text_detection` | All disabled | OCR engines for finding elements by on-screen text. |
| `image_detection` | All disabled | Engines for finding elements by image templates. |
| `llm_models` | All disabled | The LLM for AI self-heal and the plain-English mode of `optics live`. |
| `log_level` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` or `CRITICAL`, any case. Unknown values become `INFO`. |
| `file_log` | `false` | Writes `internal_logs.log` and `execution_logs.log` to the output folder. |
| `log_path` | None | One file for both logs instead of two. Used only with `file_log: true`. |
| `json_log` | `false` | Writes a JSON array of every test, module and keyword event to `logs.json` at the end of the run. |
| `json_path` | None | Where to write the JSON events instead of `<output>/logs.json`. `~` is expanded. |
| `console` | `true` | **Has no effect in 1.10.5.** Nothing reads it. Use `log_level` to control console output. |
| `execution_output_path` | `<project>/execution_output` | Where results, screenshots and logs go. Relative paths are relative to the folder you run `optics` from. |
| `include` | None | Run only these test cases. See [include and exclude](#include-and-exclude). |
| `exclude` | None | Skip these test cases. |
| `ai_self_heal` | `false` | Lets an LLM try to recover when an element can't be found. See [ai_self_heal](#ai-self-heal). |
| `strict_element_match` | `false` | Turns off fuzzy and partial text matching. See [strict_element_match](#strict-element-match). |
| `save_captures` | `true` | Whether `Capture Screenshot`, `Capture Pagesource` and `Get Screen Elements` write files. See [save_captures](#save-captures). |
| `halt_duration` | `0.1` | Seconds to wait after a keyword fails every fallback. It isn't a pause between steps. |
| `event_attributes_json` | None | Path to a JSON file of event attributes. When it includes an `eventUrl`, events you label with `event_name` are sent there at the end of the session. |
| `project_path` | The project folder | The CLI always sets this to the folder you pass, so leave it out. It only matters for the Python SDK. |

**Note:**
If you set `execution_output_path` yourself, create the folder first. JUnit results and logs create their own folders, but screenshots fail to save without a warning if the folder is missing.

## Engine lists

`driver_sources`, `elements_sources`, `text_detection`, `image_detection` and `llm_models` are lists. Each item is an engine name with its settings:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:                 # engine name
      enabled: true         # required: only enabled entries are loaded
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"
      capabilities:         # engine-specific settings
        platformName: Android
```

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | Required | Only enabled entries are loaded. A disabled entry with any name is ignored. |
| `url` | None | The server address, for engines that use one. |
| `capabilities` | `{}` | Settings passed to the engine. |

When several entries in one list are enabled, Optics tries them in the order you list them. For element sources this is the order in which strategies run.

An enabled entry with an unknown name fails with [E0601](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e06-modules-and-engines). So does an enabled engine whose extra isn't installed. A list you write replaces the default list completely.

### driver_sources

Enable one driver. `optics live` refuses more than one, and `optics doctor` warns about it.

| Name | Extra | What it drives |
|---|---|---|
| `appium` | `appium` | Android, iOS, Android TV, Samsung Tizen TV and LG webOS TV apps through an Appium server. |
| `selenium` | `selenium` | Chrome or Firefox through a Selenium server or Grid. |
| `playwright` | `playwright` | A local Chromium browser. No server needed. |
| `ble` | `ble` | Any device paired with a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle. For devices with no automation access. |

### elements_sources

Enable the sources that match your driver. We recommend all three for your driver: locators, page source and screenshots.

| Name | Needs driver | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| `appium_find_element` | `appium` | Finds elements by XPath, accessibility id and class. |
| `appium_page_source` | `appium` | Searches the UI tree by XPath and text, with fuzzy matching. Lists interactive elements. |
| `appium_screenshot` | `appium` | Screenshots for OCR, image matching and AI self-heal. |
| `selenium_find_element` | `selenium` | Finds elements by XPath, text, id, name, CSS and link text. |
| `selenium_page_source` | `selenium` | Searches the page HTML. Doesn't list interactive elements. |
| `selenium_screenshot` | `selenium` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. |
| `playwright_find_element` | `playwright` | Finds elements by `xpath=`, `css=` and `text=` locators. |
| `playwright_page_source` | `playwright` | Searches the page and lists interactive elements. |
| `playwright_screenshot` | `playwright` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. |
| `camera_screenshot` | Any | Frames from a webcam or a TCP frame server. Used with `ble`. |

`optics doctor` fails a project when no enabled element source starts with the enabled driver's name.

### text_detection

| Name | Extra | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| `easyocr` | `easyocr` | None. Accurate but slow on CPU. Downloads its models on first use. The language is always English. |
| `pytesseract` | `pytesseract` | None. Needs the Tesseract program installed and on your PATH. |
| `google_vision` | `google-vision` | None. Credentials come from `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. `googlevision` also works. |
| `remote_ocr` | None | `url` (required): your OCR service. `capabilities`: `timeout` (30), `method` (`easyocr`), `language` (`en`). Optics posts screenshots to `<url>/detect-text`. |

### image_detection

| Name | Extra | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| `templatematch` | None | `capabilities.sift_nfeatures` (2000). Finds template images, including scaled or rotated ones. Images are found by file name anywhere in the project. |
| `remote_oir` | None | `url` (required): your image service. `capabilities`: `timeout` (30), `method` (`template_matching`). Optics posts to `<url>/detect-image`. |

### llm_models

Optics supports three LLM engines: `gemini`, `openai` and `anthropic`. Each has an extra of the same name, and the `llm` bundle installs all three. Use environment variables for keys, not `config.yaml`. If you enable more than one entry, Optics tries them in list order and moves to the next when a call fails.

#### gemini

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | The Gemini model. |
| `use_vertexai` | From `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` | `true` uses Vertex AI instead of the Gemini API. |
| `project`, `location` | From `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` | The Vertex AI project and region. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |

```yaml
llm_models:
  - gemini:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        model: gemini-2.5-flash
```

Gemini reads its key from `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. For Vertex AI, set `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true` with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. Optics accepts `api_key` in `capabilities` too, but warns when you use it.

#### openai

Works with OpenAI and any server that offers an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. Set the entry's `url` to the server's base URL, or leave it out to call OpenAI. `OPENAI_BASE_URL` works in place of `url`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | None (required) | The model name as the server spells it, for example `gpt-5-mini`, or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` on OpenRouter. |
| `api_key_env` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | The environment variable that holds the key. |
| `response_format` | `json_schema` | Set `json_object` if the server rejects JSON-schema output. Optics then puts the schema in the prompt instead. |
| `max_tokens` | The server's limit | The longest reply the model may write. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |

| Server | `url` | Key |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | Leave it out | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, with `api_key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| Azure OpenAI | `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/` | Your Azure key, in the variable named by `api_key_env` |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | None |
| vLLM, LM Studio | The server's `/v1` URL | None |

```yaml
llm_models:
  - openai:
      enabled: true
      url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
      capabilities:
        model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
        api_key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
```

#### anthropic

Use Claude through the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. For Bedrock or Vertex AI, also install `anthropic[bedrock]` or `anthropic[vertex]` into the same Python environment as Optics.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | None (required) | The model ID, for example `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Bedrock and Vertex AI use their own model IDs. |
| `platform` | `anthropic` | `anthropic` (the Claude API), `bedrock` or `vertex`. |
| `region` | From the environment | The Bedrock or Vertex AI region. |
| `project` | From the environment | The Vertex AI project. |
| `api_key_env` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | The environment variable that holds the Claude API key. |
| `max_tokens` | `4096` | The longest reply the model may write. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |

| Platform | Credentials |
|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or the variable `api_key_env` names |
| `bedrock` | Your usual AWS credentials, such as `AWS_PROFILE` and `AWS_REGION` |
| `vertex` | Google Cloud application default credentials |

## Examples by platform

**Android**

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"        # required; the Appium server
      capabilities:                        # must not be empty
        platformName: Android              # required; picks the Android profile
        automationName: UiAutomator2
        deviceName: emulator-5554
        # udid: emulator-5554              # pin one device when several are connected
        appPackage: com.birch.shop         # the app Launch App opens
        appActivity: com.birch.shop.MainActivity
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}   # XPath, accessibility id, class
  - appium_page_source:  {enabled: true}   # UI tree search (uses strict_element_match)
  - appium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}   # screenshots for OCR, images, self-heal
text_detection:
  - easyocr: {enabled: true}               # extra: easyocr
image_detection:
  - templatematch: {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
file_log: true
json_log: true
```

Before `optics execute`, Optics checks that the Appium server answers and that `adb devices` lists a device.
**iOS**

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: iOS                  # picks the iOS profile
        automationName: XCUITest
        deviceName: "iPhone 15"
        bundleId: com.birch.shop           # required on iOS
        # udid: <device udid>              # for a real device
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - appium_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - appium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
file_log: true
```

`optics doctor` fails an iOS project without `bundleId`. The preflight checks only the Appium server.
**Web**

Use Playwright unless you already run a Selenium Grid. It needs no server.

`config.yaml (Playwright)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - playwright:
      enabled: true                        # no url and no server
      capabilities:
        browser: chromium                  # currently ignored, see the note below
        headless: false                    # currently ignored
elements_sources:
  - playwright_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - playwright_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - playwright_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
```

**Note:**
In 1.10.5 the Playwright driver ignores `browser`, `headless` and `viewport` under `capabilities`. It always opens a visible Chromium window at 1280×800, and waits up to 60 seconds for each page to load.

Open your site with a module step such as `Launch App,https://birch.example`.

`config.yaml (Selenium)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - selenium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4444/wd/hub"  # the Selenium server or Grid
      capabilities:                        # must not be empty
        browserName: chrome                # required: chrome or firefox
        browserURL: "https://birch.example"  # opened when the session starts
elements_sources:
  - selenium_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - selenium_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - selenium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
```

Selenium won't start with empty `capabilities` or without `browserName`. The file `optics configure` writes for `web-selenium` has `capabilities: {}`, so add `browserName` before you run.

### Appium capabilities

Optics reads only `platformName` and the app id; it passes every other capability to Appium unchanged. You can write any key with the `appium:` prefix, for example `appium:udid`.

| platformName | App id capability | Defaults Optics adds (your values win) |
|---|---|---|
| `Android` | `appPackage` and `appActivity` | `noReset`, `newCommandTimeout: 3600`, `forceAppLaunch`, `shouldTerminateApp`, `ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError` and a few others |
| `iOS` | `bundleId` | The same mobile defaults, without `ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError` |
| `TizenTV` | `appPackage` | `newCommandTimeout: 3600`, `rcMode: remote`, `noReset: true` |
| `LGTV` | `appId` | `newCommandTimeout: 600`, `rcMode: rc`, `useSecureWebsocket: true`, `autoExtendDevMode: false`, `noReset: true` |

Any other `platformName` fails with [E0104](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e01-driver-and-session). To attach to an Appium session that's already running, add `appium:existingSessionId`. Optics starts a new session if it can't attach.

## TV

Android TV uses the Android example. Samsung and LG TVs use Appium's TV drivers:

`config.yaml (Samsung Tizen)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: TizenTV
        appium:automationName: TizenTV
        appium:deviceAddress: 192.168.1.50
        appium:rcToken: "14184553"
        appium:appPackage: com.birch.tv
        appium:app: /path/to/birch.wgt
        appium:chromedriverExecutableDir: /path/to/chromedrivers
elements_sources:
  - appium_page_source: {enabled: true}
  - appium_screenshot:  {enabled: true}
```

`config.yaml (LG webOS)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: LGTV
        appium:automationName: webOS
        appium:deviceHost: 192.168.1.50
        appium:appId: com.birch.tv
elements_sources:
  - appium_screenshot: {enabled: true}
```

On Tizen and webOS, touch and typing keywords fail with [E0105](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e01-driver-and-session). Move around with `Press Keycode` and remote keys: `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `ENTER`, `BACK`, `HOME`, `PLAY`, `PAUSE`, `STOP`, `REWIND`, `FF`. See [Test TV apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv).

## BLE and camera

The `ble` driver taps and types through a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle. A camera or frame server provides the screen, and Optics finds elements with OCR or image templates.

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - ble:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        device_id: "Birch test phone"     # required
        port: "/dev/ttyACM0"              # required: device path, COM port or USB product name
        pixel_width: 1080                 # the device screen in pixels
        pixel_height: 2336
        mickeys_width: 1080               # the device screen in mouse units
        mickeys_height: 2336
        x_invert: 1                       # 1 or -1
        y_invert: 1
elements_sources:
  - camera_screenshot:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        camera_index: 0                   # a webcam, or url: "192.168.1.20:9000" for a TCP frame server
text_detection:
  - easyocr: {enabled: true}
image_detection:
  - templatematch: {enabled: true}
```

| `ble` capability | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `device_id` | Required | A name for the device. |
| `port` | Required | The dongle's serial port (`/dev/ttyACM0`, `COM3`) or its USB product description. |
| `pixel_width`, `pixel_height` | `0` | The device screen size in pixels. Set them: taps can't be placed without them. |
| `mickeys_width`, `mickeys_height` | `0` | The device screen size in mouse movement units. Set them too. |
| `x_invert`, `y_invert` | `1` | `-1` reverses the direction of mouse movement on that axis. |

| `camera_screenshot` capability | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `camera_index` | None | The webcam number. Use this or `url`. |
| `url` | None | A TCP frame server as `host:port`. |
| `header_size` | `8` | Bytes in the frame server's length header: `4` or `8`. |
| `byte_order` | `little` | The length header's byte order: `little` or `big`. |

The BLE driver can't launch apps, so `Launch App` fails. Open the app by hand or with keys before the run. XPath and text locators don't work without a UI tree; use text that OCR can read, or image templates. See [Test production devices](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/production).

## include and exclude

Run a subset of test cases. There are no CLI flags for this.

```yaml
include:
  - Shopper can sign in
  - Shopper can add Trail Runner 2 to the cart
# or
exclude:
  - Shopper can check out
```

- Names match the `test_case` column exactly, ignoring case.
- Set one of the two. Setting both fails with [E0403](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e04-keywords-and-parameters).
- Test cases with "setup" or "teardown" in their names always run.

## Logging

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `log_level` | `INFO` | The level for the console and the log files. Set `DEBUG` to see every strategy Optics tries. |
| `file_log` | `false` | Writes `internal_logs.log` and `execution_logs.log` to the output folder. Each rotates at 10 MB and keeps 10 old files. |
| `log_path` | None | Sends both logs to this one file. |
| `json_log` | `false` | Writes `logs.json`: a list of events with name, status, timings and log lines for each test case, module and keyword. |
| `json_path` | None | Writes the JSON events here instead. |
| `console` | `true` | No effect in 1.10.5. |

With `file_log: true` and no `execution_output_path`, Optics also writes a copy of both logs to `logs/` in the folder you ran `optics` from.

Values you write with the `@:` prefix, such as `@:s3cret`, are masked as `****` in log files. See [Read results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).

## ai_self_heal

When an element can't be found, self-heal sends a screenshot to an LLM and lets it try up to five corrective steps, such as scrolling or closing a popup.

```yaml
ai_self_heal: true
llm_models:
  - gemini:
      enabled: true
```

- It needs an enabled `llm_models` entry, that engine's extra and key, and a screenshot element source such as `appium_screenshot`. Without them it does nothing, and the run isn't affected.
- It applies to keywords that find and act on an element: `Press Element`, `Enter Text`, `Enter Number`, `Clear Element Text`, `Get Text`, `Swipe From Element`, `Scroll From Element`, `Detect And Press` and `Select Dropdown Option`. It doesn't apply to assertions.
- A healed step passes. Check the logs for `AI self-heal:` lines so a real regression doesn't go unnoticed.

`optics serve` and `optics mcp` ignore this key. They use per-session fields and the `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` variable instead. See [Self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal).

## strict_element_match

```yaml
strict_element_match: true
```

By default the page-source element sources (`appium_page_source`, `selenium_page_source`, `playwright_page_source`) accept close or partial text matches, so `Sign in` can match `Sign in with email`. Set `strict_element_match: true` to accept only exact matches. Turn it on when similar labels make tests press the wrong element.

## save_captures

```yaml
save_captures: false
```

When `false`, `Capture Screenshot`, `Capture Pagesource` and `Get Screen Elements` stop writing files. Optics still saves the screenshot it takes before each action, the annotated screenshots and the page source logs. `optics serve` always turns captures off.

## Starter config

`optics init` writes a commented config.yaml with every engine disabled. To get started, enable one driver, enable its three element sources, and install the driver's extra with `optics setup --install <name>`. See [Install Optics](https://optics-framework.org/docs/get-started/install).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files

# Project files

> The file formats Optics reads: test cases, modules, elements, error definitions and API definitions.

An Optics project is a folder of CSV or YAML files plus a config.yaml. This page lists every file format Optics reads, the exact columns and keys, and what a run writes back.

For a guided introduction, see [Write a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/write) and [Write tests in YAML](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/yaml).

## How Optics finds your files

Optics walks the whole project folder, including subfolders, and decides what each `.csv`, `.yml` and `.yaml` file is by its **content**, not its name or location. You can use any folder layout. We recommend the one `optics init` creates:

```tree
birch-tests/
├── config.yaml
├── test_cases/test_cases.csv
├── modules/modules.csv
├── test_data/elements.csv
└── test_data/error_definitions.csv    # optional
```

| File type | CSV: the header row must contain | YAML: top-level key |
|---|---|---|
| Test cases | `test_case` and `test_step` | `Test Cases` |
| Modules | `module_name` and `module_step` | `Modules` |
| Elements | `Element_Name` and `Element_ID` | `Elements` |
| Error definitions | `error_code` and `match_string` | Not supported |
| API definitions | Not supported | `api` |
| Config | Not applicable | `driver_sources` and `elements_sources` |

A project needs at least one test cases file and one modules file. Elements, error definitions and API files are optional. You can split each type across several files.

**Common mistake:**
Write column names and YAML keys exactly as shown. Optics recognizes `element_name` or `test_cases:` as the right file type, but then reads nothing from it, because the reader expects `Element_Name` and `Test Cases`.

When two files define the same thing:

- **Test cases** and **modules** with the same name: the file read last wins, with a warning in the log.
- **Elements** with the same name: the values are combined into one fallback list.

Image files (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.bmp`) anywhere in the project are available as image templates by file name. If two images share a name, one of them is used.

## Test cases

Each row adds one step to a test case. A step names a module. Rows run in order, and a test case can span rows anywhere in the file.

**CSV**

`test_cases/test_cases.csv`:

```csv
test_case,test_step
Suite Setup,Open Birch
Shopper can sign in,Sign In
Shopper can sign in,Check Home Screen
Shopper can add a shoe,Search For Trail Runner
Shopper can add a shoe,Add To Cart
Suite Teardown,Close Birch
```
**YAML**

`test_cases/test_cases.yaml`:

```yaml
Test Cases:
  - Suite Setup:
      - Open Birch
  - Shopper can sign in:
      - Sign In
      - Check Home Screen
  - Shopper can add a shoe:
      - Search For Trail Runner
      - Add To Cart
  - Suite Teardown:
      - Close Birch
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `test_case` | The test case name. Rows with an empty name are skipped. |
| `test_step` | The name of a module to run. Rows with an empty step are skipped. |

Within a test case, the first failing step fails the test case and skips its remaining steps. The next test case still runs.

**Warning:**
A `test_step` that names a keyword instead of a module passes both `dry_run` and `execute` but runs nothing. Put keywords in a module and name the module here.

### Setup and teardown

Optics treats some test case names specially. Matching ignores case and looks for the words anywhere in the name.

| Name contains | Role | When it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `suite` and `setup` | Suite setup | Once, before every other test case. If several match, the last one is used. |
| `suite` and `teardown` | Suite teardown | Once, after every other test case. |
| `setup` without `suite` | Per-test setup | Meant to run before each test. In 1.10.5 it runs only before the first test case. |
| `teardown` without `suite` | Per-test teardown | Meant to run after each test. In 1.10.5 it runs only after the first test case. |

We recommend `Suite Setup` and `Suite Teardown`, which work as expected. Avoid per-test `Setup` and `Teardown` until this is fixed; open and close the app inside each test case's own modules if you need that.

- A failing setup doesn't stop the test cases after it.
- Test cases whose names contain "setup" or "teardown" always run, even when `include` or `exclude` would skip them.
- Don't use "setup" or "teardown" in an ordinary test name. "Setup wizard works" is treated as the per-test setup.

## Modules

Each row is one keyword step. A module is the rows that share a `module_name`, in order.

**CSV**

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3
Open Birch,Launch App,,,
Sign In,Assert Presence,${email_field},20,
Sign In,Enter Text,${email_field},ana@birch.example,
Sign In,Enter Text,${password_field},@:s3cret,
Sign In,Press Element,${sign_in},,
Search For Trail Runner,Press Element,${search_bar},,
Search For Trail Runner,Enter Text,${search_bar},Trail Runner 2,
Add To Cart,Press Element,${add_to_cart},index=0,
Close Birch,Close And Terminate App,,,
```
**YAML**

`modules/modules.yaml`:

```yaml
Modules:
  - Open Birch:
      - Launch App
  - Sign In:
      - Assert Presence ${email_field} 20
      - Enter Text ${email_field} ana@birch.example
      - Enter Text ${password_field} @:s3cret
      - Press Element ${sign_in}
  - Search For Trail Runner:
      - Press Element ${search_bar}
      - Enter Text ${search_bar} "Trail Runner 2"
  - Add To Cart:
      - Press Element ${add_to_cart} index=0
  - Close Birch:
      - Close And Terminate App
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `module_name` | The module name. |
| `module_step` | A keyword name, such as `Press Element`. Case and spaces don't matter: `press_element` works too. To run another module from inside a module, use `Execute Module,<name>`. |
| `param_1`, `param_2`, … | The keyword's parameters, in order. Add as many `param_` columns as you need. |

Parameter rules:

- **Empty cells are dropped**, and the values after them move left. You can't skip a parameter by leaving its cell blank. Use a named parameter instead.
- **Named parameters** are written `name=value`, for example `index=0` or `timeout_str=20`. They work only when `name` is a real parameter of that keyword. Anything else, such as `text=Sign in` or `css=#search`, stays a positional value.
- **Variables** written as a whole cell, `${email_field}`, are replaced with the element's values. `Hello ${name}` isn't substituted; Optics types it as written.
- Values starting with `/`, `//` or `(` are always positional, so XPaths are never mistaken for named parameters.

In YAML, a step is one string. The keyword name is matched first, and the rest is split on spaces. Wrap a value with spaces in quotes: `"Trail Runner 2"`. Wrap multi-word module names you pass as parameters in quotes too: `Run Loop "Add To Cart" 3`.

See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/) for each keyword's parameters.

## Elements

Each row gives a name to a locator or a value. Steps refer to it as `${name}`.

**CSV**

`test_data/elements.csv`:

```csv
Element_Name,Element_ID,Element_ID_text,Element_ID_image
email_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/email'],Email,
password_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/password'],Password,
sign_in,//android.widget.Button[@text='Sign in'],Sign in,sign_in.png
search_bar,//*[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/search'],Search,
add_to_cart,text=Add to cart,,add_to_cart.png
order_total,placeholder,,
```
**YAML**

`test_data/elements.yaml`:

```yaml
Elements:
  email_field:
    - //android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/email']
    - Email
  sign_in: ["//android.widget.Button[@text='Sign in']", "Sign in", "sign_in.png"]
  search_bar: "//*[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/search']"
  add_to_cart: ["text=Add to cart", "add_to_cart.png"]
  order_total: placeholder
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Element_Name` | The name. Write the header exactly like this. |
| `Element_ID` | The first locator or value. Required. |
| `Element_ID_*` | Fallbacks. Any column whose header starts with `Element_ID`, such as `Element_ID_text`, `Element_ID_image` or `Element_ID_2`, adds another value. They're tried in column order. |

- Empty cells are ignored. Columns that don't start with `Element_ID`, such as `Element_Text`, are ignored.
- A second row with the same name adds more fallback values.
- When a step uses `${name}`, Optics tries each value in turn until the step passes, up to 20 attempts. It moves on only when the element isn't found. Steps inside `Run Loop`, `Condition` and `Execute Module` use only the first value.
- Variables a step creates while running, such as the target of `Evaluate` or `Read Data`, need a row with a placeholder value so `optics dry_run` passes.

Optics decides what kind of locator a value is from its form:

| Value | Treated as |
|---|---|
| Starts with `text=` or `text_only:` | Text. `text_only:` uses OCR only. |
| Ends with `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.bmp` | An image template, found by file name anywhere in the project. |
| Starts with `css=` | CSS selector. |
| Starts with `xpath=`, `/`, `//` or `(` | XPath. |
| Starts with `android.` or `xcui` | A UI class name. |
| Starts with `.` or `#`, or contains `[` and `]` | CSS selector. |
| Anything else | Text. |

Text like `(optional)` or `Size [US]` is read as XPath or CSS. Add `text=` in front to force text: `text=Size [US]`. See [Define elements](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/define).

## Error definitions

A CSV file of messages that mean your app is in a bad state. At the end of `optics execute`, Optics checks the text on the final screen against each `match_string`.

`test_data/error_definitions.csv`:

```csv
error_code,match_string,description,severity
BIRCH_001,Unfortunately,App crashed with a system dialog,critical
BIRCH_002,Something went wrong,Birch showed its generic error screen,high
BIRCH_003,Out of stock,Product page shows out of stock,medium
```

| Column | Required | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `error_code` | Yes | Your code for this error. A repeated code replaces the earlier row. |
| `match_string` | Yes | Text to look for. Matching ignores case and finds the text anywhere in the screen's text. It isn't a regular expression. |
| `description` | No | Free text, shown in the results. |
| `severity` | No | Free text, for example `critical`, `high` or `medium`. |

There's no YAML form. A match adds a failing test case to `junit_output.xml` but doesn't change the exit code. See [Detect on-screen errors](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/error-detection).

## API definitions

A YAML file with a top-level `api:` key defines HTTP calls that the `Invoke API` keyword makes. You can also put the `api:` block inside config.yaml.

`test_data/api.yaml`:

```yaml
api:
  collections:
    birch:                                  # collection id, used in Invoke API
      name: Birch API
      base_url: https://api.birch.example
      global_headers:
        Accept: application/json
      apis:
        get_product:                        # API id
          name: Get product
          description: Look up Trail Runner 2
          endpoint: /v1/products/trail-runner-2
          request:
            method: GET
            headers: {}
            body: null
          expected_result:
            jsonpath_assertions:
              - path: $.name
                condition: "$ == 'Trail Runner 2'"
            extract:
              product_price: $.price        # saves ${product_price}
```

Call it from a module with `Invoke API,birch.get_product`. Only the top-level key `api` works; a file whose top key is `apis` is recognized but loads nothing. See [Call an API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/api-calls).

## Escaping and special values

**CSV quoting.** Wrap a cell in double quotes when it contains a comma, and double any quotes inside it:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1
Find Shoe,Press Element,"//*[contains(@text,'Trail Runner 2')]"
Go Home,Execute Script,"{""script"": ""mobile: pressKey"", ""args"": {""keycode"": 3}}"
```

**Backslash sequences.** In any cell, `\n` becomes a new line, `\t` a tab, `\r` a carriage return, and `\\` a single backslash.

**Secrets.** Start a value with `@:`, as in `@:s3cret`, to mask it as `****` in log files. Optics removes the prefix before typing.

**Encoding.** Save files as UTF-8. Some spreadsheet apps add a byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file, which can stop Optics recognizing the header row.

**YAML quoting.** A quoted value that contains `=` keeps its quotes. Write conditions without spaces instead: `Condition ${size}=='9' "Pick Size" "Show Error"`.

## Outputs

`optics execute` and `optics dry_run` write to `execution_output/` in the project, unless you set `execution_output_path` in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config).

```tree
birch-tests/execution_output/
├── junit_output.xml
├── logs.json                                      # json_log: true
├── internal_logs.log                              # file_log: true
├── execution_logs.log                             # file_log: true
├── 2026-10-09T15-04-05-123456-pre_press_element.jpg
├── ...-press_element_element_detection_result.jpg
├── ...-end_of_run.jpg
├── page_sources_log.xml
└── detected_errors_<session_id>.json              # only when error definitions match
```

| File | When it's written | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `junit_output.xml` | Every run, including dry runs | One test case per test, with each module and keyword, their status, timings and log lines. Error detection adds a failing `on-screen-error-detection` test case. If another session is already writing the file, Optics names it `junit_output_<session_id>.xml`. |
| `logs.json` | `json_log: true` | A JSON list of every test case, module and keyword event with status and timings. |
| `internal_logs.log`, `execution_logs.log` | `file_log: true` | Text logs. Each rotates at 10 MB. |
| `<time>-pre_<keyword>.jpg` | Every keyword that finds an element | The screen before Optics looked for the element. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_element_detection_result.jpg` | An element was found in the UI tree | The screen with a green box around the element. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_image_detection_result.jpg` | An element was found by OCR or image | The screen with a green box, and a red dot at the tap point for text. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_with_aoi.jpg` | The step used an area of interest | The screen with the area drawn in blue. |
| `<time>-<keyword>.jpg` | Gestures and coordinate keywords, such as `Swipe`, `Scroll`, `Press By Percentage`, `Press Keycode` | The screen when the step ran. |
| `<time>-capture_screenshot.jpg` | `Capture Screenshot`, `Get Screen Elements` | Only when `save_captures` is `true`. |
| `<time>-end_of_run.jpg` | End of `optics execute`, if the app is still open | The final screen. |
| `page_sources_log.xml` | Appium page source reads and the end of the run | Each UI tree, with a timestamp. |
| `page_sources_log.html` | Selenium page source reads and the end of the run | Each page's HTML, with a timestamp. |
| `interactable_elements.json` | `Get Interactive Elements`, `Get Screen Elements` | The latest list of elements on screen. |
| `api_details.log`, `api_details.har` | `Invoke API` | Each request and response. |
| `detected_errors_<session_id>.json` | Error definitions matched at the end of the run | The codes, matched text, descriptions and severities. |

Screenshots are JPEG files named `<timestamp>-<name>.jpg`. The detection-result screenshots use a timestamp with colons in it, which Windows doesn't allow in file names, so they may be missing on Windows.

`optics live` writes elsewhere: `screenshots/session_<time>/` and `logs/optics_live_<time>.log` in the project. See [Read results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines

# Engines and extras

> Learn which drivers, element sources, OCR, image matching and LLM engines Optics supports, and which pip extra installs each one.

Optics keeps its core install small. Each driver and recognition engine is a separate pip extra that you add for your platform, either with [`optics setup`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#optics-setup) or with pip. You then turn the engine on by name in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists).

The name you write in config.yaml is the engine's name in the tables below. The extra is what you install.

## Drivers

A driver controls the device or browser. Enable one under `driver_sources`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appium` | `appium` | Native and hybrid apps through an Appium server. | Android, iOS, Android TV, Samsung Tizen TV, LG webOS TV |
| `selenium` | `selenium` | Websites through a Selenium server or Grid. Chrome and Firefox only. | Web |
| `playwright` | `playwright` | Websites in a local Chromium browser, with no server to run. | Web |
| `ble` | `ble` | Taps and typing through a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle, for devices with no automation access. | Any device that accepts a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard |

The Appium server itself, and its UiAutomator2 or XCUITest driver, aren't Python packages. Install and start them separately. See [Test Android apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/android) and [Test iOS apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/ios).

## Element sources

An element source is how Optics looks at the screen for a driver. They need no extra of their own: they come with their driver. Enable them under `elements_sources`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appium_find_element` | `appium` | Finds elements by XPath, accessibility id or class. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `appium_page_source` | `appium` | Searches the UI tree by XPath and text. Lists interactive elements. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `appium_screenshot` | `appium` | Screenshots for OCR, image matching and AI self-heal. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `selenium_find_element` | `selenium` | Finds elements by XPath, text, id, name, CSS or link text. | Web |
| `selenium_page_source` | `selenium` | Searches the page HTML. | Web |
| `selenium_screenshot` | `selenium` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. | Web |
| `playwright_find_element` | `playwright` | Finds elements by `xpath=`, `css=` and `text=` locators. | Web |
| `playwright_page_source` | `playwright` | Searches the page and lists interactive elements. | Web |
| `playwright_screenshot` | `playwright` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. | Web |
| `camera_screenshot` | None | Frames from a webcam or a TCP frame server. | Any, usually with `ble` |

Only `appium_page_source` and `playwright_page_source` can list interactive elements. With Selenium, `Get Interactive Elements`, the HTTP `/elements` endpoint and the MCP elements resource fail with [E0202](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e02-elements).

## Text recognition (OCR)

OCR finds elements by the text visible in a screenshot. Optics uses it when the UI tree doesn't have the text, or when you write `text_only:`. Enable engines under `text_detection`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `easyocr` | `easyocr` | Local OCR. Accurate but slow on CPU. Downloads its models the first time it runs. English only. | All |
| `pytesseract` | `pytesseract` | Local OCR with Tesseract. Needs the Tesseract program installed and on your PATH. Matches whole words. | All |
| `google_vision` | `google-vision` | Google Cloud Vision. Needs Google Cloud credentials in `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. | All |
| `remote_ocr` | None | Your own OCR service over HTTP. Set its `url`. | All |

We recommend `easyocr` to start with. It needs nothing else installed.

## Image matching

Image matching finds an element by a template image you saved in the project. Enable engines under `image_detection`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `templatematch` | None | Local matching. Finds templates even when they're scaled or rotated. | All |
| `remote_oir` | None | Your own image matching service over HTTP. Set its `url`. | All |

## LLM

An LLM powers [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal) and the plain-English mode of `optics live`. Enable one under `llm_models`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gemini` | `gemini` | Google Gemini, through the Gemini API or Vertex AI. Default model `gemini-2.5-flash`. | All |
| `openai` | `openai` | OpenAI, and any server with an OpenAI-compatible API: OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI, or a local model in Ollama, vLLM or LM Studio. | All |
| `anthropic` | `anthropic` | Claude, through the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. | All |

Each engine reads its credentials from the environment. See [llm_models](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#llm-models) for its settings and credentials.

## Other extras

| Extra | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | The [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp), `optics mcp`. Install it with pip; `optics setup` can't install it, and the `all` bundle doesn't include it. |

## Bundles

A bundle installs several extras at once.

| Bundle | Installs |
|---|---|
| `mobile` | `appium` |
| `web` | `selenium`, `playwright` |
| `vision` | `easyocr`, `pytesseract`, `google-vision` |
| `llm` | `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic` |
| `all` | `appium`, `ble`, `selenium`, `playwright`, `easyocr`, `pytesseract`, `google-vision`, `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic`. Not `mcp`. |

## Install with optics setup

`optics setup` installs extras into the same Python environment Optics runs in.

```text
optics setup [--install NAME [NAME ...]] [--list]
```

Without flags, it opens a picker with a checkbox for each engine. In scripts and CI, name the engines:

```shell
$ optics setup --install appium easyocr
$ optics setup --install web gemini
$ optics setup --install appium==5.0.0
```

- Names are case-insensitive. Use an extra name, a display name such as `Gemini` or `Google Vision`, or a bundle.
- Pin the engine's main package with a version specifier: `appium==5.0.0`, `"easyocr>=1.7,<2.0"`. Use an operator such as `==`; `appium=5.0.0` is an error. Bundles can't take a version.
- Optics keeps itself at the version you have, so installing an engine never upgrades Optics.
- Installing `playwright` also downloads the Chromium browser.

`optics setup --list` prints every name:

```terminal
Available engines (install with `optics setup --install <name>`):

Action Drivers:
  appium          (appium-python-client)
  ble             (pyserial)
  selenium        (selenium)
  playwright      (playwright)

OCR Engines:
  easyocr         (easyocr)
  pytesseract     (pytesseract, pillow)
  google-vision   (google-cloud-vision)

LLM Engines:
  gemini          (google-genai)
  openai          (openai)
  anthropic       (anthropic)

Bundles (install several at once):
  mobile          (appium)
  web             (selenium, playwright)
  vision          (easyocr, pytesseract, google-vision)
  llm             (gemini, openai, anthropic)
  all             (appium, ble, selenium, playwright, easyocr, pytesseract, google-vision, gemini, openai, anthropic)

Pin a version by appending a specifier, e.g. `optics setup --install appium==5.0.0`.
```

On success, Optics reminds you that services such as the Appium server still need to be started separately. Run `optics doctor` to confirm each engine shows ✅.

## Install with pip

Name the extras in brackets:

```shell
$ pip install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"
$ pip install "optics-framework[playwright]" && playwright install chromium
$ pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"
```

If you installed Optics with the [install script](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#install-scripts), pass extras with `--extra appium,easyocr` (or `OPTICS_EXTRA` on Windows).

## Where installs are refused

`optics setup` and `optics quickstart` refuse to install into environments that another tool manages, because changing them would break that tool. `optics doctor` shows an `environment` ⚠️ row when this applies.

| Environment | What to do instead |
|---|---|
| Conda | Use a virtual environment. EasyOCR and Optics need conflicting versions of NumPy under Conda. |
| `pipx` | Reinstall with the extras: `pipx install --force "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"`, or add packages with `pipx inject optics-framework <package>`. |
| `uv tool` or `uvx` | Reinstall with the extras: `uv tool install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"`. |
| A project managed by uv, Poetry, PDM or Pipenv | Add the extra with your tool, for example `uv add "optics-framework[appium]"` or `poetry add "optics-framework[appium]"`. |
| System Python marked as externally managed | Use a virtual environment. |
| Read-only site-packages | Use a virtual environment you can write to. |
| No pip and no uv | Install pip, or use a virtual environment. |

To create a virtual environment:

**macOS and Linux**

```shell
$ python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install optics-framework
```
**Windows**

```powershell
PS> python -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1; pip install optics-framework
```

In a virtual environment without pip, `optics setup` uses `uv` if it's available.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp

# MCP server reference

> Tools and resources that `optics mcp` gives your AI agent.

`optics mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, a standard way for AI agents such as Claude, Cursor or VS Code to call outside tools. Your agent can start a session on a device or browser, look at the screen, and run Optics keywords one at a time.

For a guided walkthrough, see [Build tests with an AI agent](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/agent).

## Install

The server needs the `mcp` extra. The [install scripts](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#install-scripts) always include it. With pip, add it yourself: `optics setup` can't install it, and the `all` bundle doesn't include it.

```shell
$ pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"
```

You also need the extras for your driver, for example `appium` or `playwright`. See [Engines and extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines).

## Start the server

```text
optics mcp [--transport stdio|http] [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio`: your agent starts the server and talks to it directly. `http`: the server listens at `http://<host>:<port>/mcp`. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--port` | `8090` | The port to listen on. `http` only. |

We recommend `stdio` for an agent on your own machine. Use `http` when the server runs in a container or on another machine.

## Connect your agent

Most agents read a JSON file that lists MCP servers. For Claude Desktop it's `claude_desktop_config.json`; for Claude Code it's `.mcp.json` in your project. Other agents use the same shape.

`.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "optics": {
      "command": "optics",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

If your agent can't find `optics`, use the full path to it, for example `/Users/ana/.optics/bin/optics`.

For the `http` transport, point the agent at the URL instead:

`.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "optics": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

When the server runs in Docker and Appium runs on your machine, pass `url: "http://host.docker.internal:4723"` to `start_session`.

## Session tools

### start_session

Starts a session and launches the app. Returns `{"session_id", "driver_id"}`. Keep the `session_id`: every other tool needs it.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver` | `appium` | `appium`, `selenium`, `playwright` or `ble`. |
| `url` | Appium: `http://127.0.0.1:4723` | The driver's server URL. |
| `capabilities` | None | The driver's capabilities, as in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform). |
| `elements_sources` | The driver's three sources | For example `["appium_find_element", "appium_page_source", "appium_screenshot"]`. Passing `[]` makes the session fail to start. |
| `text_detection` | None | OCR engines, for example `["easyocr"]`. |
| `image_detection` | None | Image engines, for example `["templatematch"]`. |
| `project_path` | None | A project folder. Optics loads its image templates. It doesn't load elements or test cases. |
| `ai_self_heal` | `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL`, else off | Turns on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal). |
| `llm_provider` | `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER`, else `gemini` | The LLM engine for self-heal: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `llm_model` | `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL`, else `gemini-2.5-flash` for Gemini | The model for self-heal. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `strict_element_match` | Off | Accepts only exact text matches. |

The first session against a remote device farm can take 30 to 60 seconds to start.

### terminate_session

Closes the app and ends the session. Takes `session_id`. Returns `{"session_id", "status": "terminated"}`.

### screenshot

Returns the current screen as a PNG image. Takes `session_id`.

## Keyword tools

Every app, action and verification keyword is a tool named after the keyword in snake_case. Each takes `session_id` plus the keyword's parameters. All parameter values are strings. Leave out a parameter to use its default.

`aoi_*` stands for `aoi_x`, `aoi_y`, `aoi_width` and `aoi_height`, an area of the screen in percent (0–100). See [Area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest).

| Tool | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `launch_app` | `app_identifier`, `app_activity`, `event_name` |
| `launch_other_app` | `app_name`, `event_name` |
| `close_and_terminate_app` | none |
| `force_terminate_app` | `app_name`, `event_name` |
| `get_app_version` | `app_package` |
| `get_driver_session_id` | none |
| `start_appium_session` | `event_name` |
| `initialise_setup` | none |

| Tool | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `press_element` | `element`, `repeat` (1), `offset_x` (0), `offset_y` (0), `index` (0), `aoi_*`, `event_name` |
| `detect_and_press` | `element`, `timeout` (30), `event_name` |
| `select_dropdown_option` | `element`, `option`, `timeout` (30), `event_name` |
| `enter_text` | `element`, `text`, `aoi_*`, `event_name`, `index` (0) |
| `enter_text_direct` | `text`, `event_name` |
| `enter_text_using_keyboard` | `text_input`, `event_name` |
| `enter_number` | `element`, `number`, `aoi_*`, `event_name`, `index` (0) |
| `clear_element_text` | `element`, `aoi_*`, `event_name`, `index` (0) |
| `get_text` | `element`, `index` (0), `aoi_*` |
| `press_keycode` | `keycode`, `event_name` |
| `swipe` | `coor_x`, `coor_y`, `direction` (right), `swipe_length` (50), `event_name` |
| `swipe_by_percentage` | `percent_x`, `percent_y`, `direction` (right), `swipe_length` (50), `event_name` |
| `swipe_from_element` | `element`, `direction`, `swipe_length`, `aoi_*`, `event_name`, `index` (0) |
| `swipe_until_element_appears` | `element`, `direction`, `timeout`, `event_name` |
| `scroll` | `direction`, `event_name` |
| `scroll_from_element` | `element`, `direction`, `scroll_length`, `aoi_*`, `event_name`, `index` (0) |
| `scroll_until_element_appears` | `element`, `direction`, `timeout`, `event_name` |
| `sleep` | `duration` |
| `execute_script` | `script_or_json`, `event_name` |
| `press_checkbox`, `press_radio_button`, `swipe_seekbar_to_right_android` | Deprecated. Use `press_element` and `swipe_from_element`. |

| Tool | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `validate_element` | `element`, `timeout` (10), `rule` (all), `event_name` |
| `is_element` | `element`, `element_state`, `timeout`, `event_name` |
| `assert_presence` | `elements`, `timeout_str` (30), `rule` (any), `event_name`, `fail` (True) |
| `assert_visibility` | `elements`, `timeout_str` (30), `rule` (any), `event_name`, `fail` (True) |
| `assert_equality` | `output`, `expression`, `event_name` |
| `validate_screen` | `elements`, `timeout` (30), `rule` (any), `event_name` |
| `get_interactive_elements` | `filter_config`, `compact` (False) |

Separate several elements with `|`, for example `elements: "text=Trail Runner 2|text=Pace Knit"`. Each tool's description in your agent comes from the keyword's own documentation. See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/) for what each parameter does.

A tool returns the keyword's result. When self-heal recovers a step, it returns `{"result", "healed": true, "heal_summary", "suggested_steps"}` instead, so your agent can write the extra steps into the test.

### Hidden coordinate taps

`press_by_coordinates` and `press_by_percentage` are hidden by default, because agents that guess coordinates write fragile tests. To expose them, set `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS=1` before you start the server.

| Tool | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `press_by_coordinates` | `coor_x`, `coor_y`, `repeat` (1), `event_name` |
| `press_by_percentage` | `percent_x`, `percent_y`, `repeat` (1), `event_name` |

## Resources

Resources are read-only data your agent can fetch by URI.

| URI | Type | What it returns |
|---|---|---|
| `optics://keywords` | JSON | Every keyword, including flow control, with its description and parameters. |
| `optics://project-format` | Markdown | How to write a CSV project: the files, columns, `${name}` variables and flow-control keywords. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/screenshot` | PNG | The current screen. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/source` | JSON | `{"page_source", "timestamp"}`: the UI tree or HTML. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/elements` | JSON | A compact list of interactive elements on screen. Appium and Playwright only. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/screen_elements` | JSON | `{"screenshot", "elements"}`: a base64 PNG and the elements in the same frame. |

`Capture Screenshot`, `Capture Pagesource` and `Get Screen Elements` aren't tools; use these resources instead. There are no MCP prompts.

## Environment variables

Set these in the environment that starts `optics mcp`. In a JSON client config, add an `env` object next to `command`.

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` | `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` turns self-heal on for every session unless `start_session` says otherwise. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER` | The default LLM engine: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL` | The default model. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS` | `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` exposes the coordinate tap tools. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | The engine's key. Keys never travel in a tool call. For Vertex AI and Bedrock, see [llm_models](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#llm-models). |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | The server the `openai` engine calls, such as OpenRouter or a local Ollama. Only the operator sets it; a session cannot. The key comes from `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `api_key_env`. |

## Typical agent loop

### Start a session
Call `start_session` with the driver, URL and capabilities, for example `driver: "appium"`, `capabilities: {"platformName": "Android", "appPackage": "com.birch.shop", ...}`. Keep the `session_id`.

### Look at the screen
Call `screenshot`, then read `optics://session/{session_id}/elements` (or call `get_interactive_elements`) for labels and positions. Read `/source` when you need XPaths.

### Act
Call keyword tools with a locator: `press_element` with `element: "text=Sign in"`, `enter_text` with an XPath, or `detect_and_press` with a visible label. Look again after each action.

### Save the run as a test
Read `optics://project-format`, then write the steps you ran into CSV files with a config.yaml. Run them with `optics execute <folder>`.

### End the session
Call `terminate_session`.

## Limits

- **No flow control.** `Run Loop`, `Condition`, `Evaluate`, `Read Data`, `Invoke API` and the other flow-control keywords aren't tools. Your agent can still write them into CSV modules for `optics execute`.
- **No recording or saving.** There are no tools to record, save, replay, find devices or run doctor. The agent writes project files itself.
- **Coordinate taps are hidden** unless you set `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS`. Self-heal can still tap by percentage when it recovers a step.
- **Sessions aren't shared.** Sessions live in the server's memory. `optics serve` and `optics live` can't see them, and restarting the server ends them.
- **Images come from a project.** There's no upload tool. Pass `project_path` to use template images.
- **Selenium has no interactive element list.** The elements resource and `get_interactive_elements` fail on Selenium; use `/source` instead.

## Errors

A failing tool returns an error message. When Optics raises a coded error, the message starts with the code in brackets, for example `[Code.E0106] Driver session is no longer active ...`. The code can carry a `Code.` prefix; it's the same code. A step that fails after trying every element value arrives as `Execution failed: All fallback attempts failed for keyword ...`, with the code inside the text. See [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api

# HTTP API reference

> Learn the endpoints `optics serve` exposes for starting sessions, running keywords and streaming results.

`optics serve` runs a local HTTP server that lets any language or tool drive a device through Optics. You start a session, send keywords one at a time, and read screenshots, UI trees and events back.

For a guided introduction, see [Drive Optics over HTTP](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/http-api). The machine-readable OpenAPI document is at [https://optics-framework.org/openapi.json](https://optics-framework.org/openapi.json).

## Start the server

```text
optics serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--workers N]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. |
| `--port` | `8000` | The port to listen on. |
| `--workers` | `1` | Server processes. Keep it at 1. Sessions live in each process's memory, so with more workers a request can reach a process that doesn't know your session and get a 404. |

The server prints its own log lines and Optics' debug logs to the terminal. Interactive docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` while it runs.

**Warning:**
The API has no authentication, and it accepts requests from any web origin (CORS is open). Anyone who can reach the port can control your devices. Keep the default `127.0.0.1`, and bind to another address only on a network you trust.

The server doesn't read config.yaml or your project's test files. Each session gets its engines from the request. Sessions also don't write screenshots or page sources to disk, and they log at `DEBUG`.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` or `/health` | Checks the server is up. Returns `{"status": "Optics Framework API is running", "version": "1.10.5"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/start` | Starts a session from a [SessionConfig](#sessionconfig) and launches the app. Returns `{"session_id", "driver_id", "status": "created"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/action` | Runs one keyword from an [ExecuteRequest](#executerequest). Returns `{"execution_id", "status": "SUCCESS", "data"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/templates` | Uploads an image template: `{"name", "image_base64"}`. The image can be raw base64 or a `data:` URL. Use the name as an element for the rest of the session. Returns `{"name", "status": "ok"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/api` | Replaces the session's API definitions for `Invoke API`. Send `{"api": {"collections": ...}}`. Returns 204. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/screenshot` | The current screen. `data.result` is a base64 PNG without a `data:` prefix, or `""` if the capture failed. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/driver-id` | The driver's own session id in `data.result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/variables` | Every variable in the session: `{"variables": {"name": ["value", ...]}}`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/elements` | Elements on screen in `data.result`. Query: `filter_config` (`all`, `interactive`, `buttons`, `inputs`, `images`, `text`; repeatable) and `compact=true`. `compact` ignores the filter. Appium and Playwright only. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/source` | The UI tree or HTML. `data` is `{"page_source", "timestamp"}` directly, not under `result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/screen_elements` | A screenshot and its elements from the same frame. `data` is `{"screenshot", "elements"}` directly, not under `result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/events` | A stream of keyword events. See [Streams](#streams). |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/stream` | A stream of screenshots and elements whenever the screen changes. See [Streams](#streams). |
| `GET` | `/v1/keywords` | Every keyword, including flow control, with its description and parameters. |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/stop` | Closes the app and ends the session. Returns `{"status": "terminated"}`. |

## SessionConfig

The body of `POST /v1/sessions/start`. Every field is optional, but a session needs a driver and at least one element source.

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver_sources` | list | The driver. Each item is a name (`"playwright"`) or `{"appium": {"url": ..., "capabilities": {...}}}`. A listed item is enabled unless it says `"enabled": false`. |
| `elements_sources` | list | Element sources by name, for example `["appium_find_element", "appium_page_source", "appium_screenshot"]`. There's no default here, so always list them. |
| `text_detection` | list | OCR engines, for example `["easyocr"]`. |
| `image_detection` | list | Image engines, for example `["templatematch"]`. |
| `project_path` | string | A project folder on the server. Optics loads its image templates. It doesn't load elements or test cases. |
| `api_data` | object | API definitions for `Invoke API`, inline. File paths aren't supported. |
| `ai_self_heal` | boolean | Turns on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal). Defaults to `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL`, else off. |
| `llm_provider` | string | The self-heal engine: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. Defaults to `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER`, else `gemini`. |
| `llm_model` | string | The self-heal model. Defaults to `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL`, else `gemini-2.5-flash` for Gemini. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `strict_element_match` | boolean | Accepts only exact text matches. |
| `appium_url`, `appium_config` | | Deprecated. Use `driver_sources`. |

Engine names are the same as in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists). LLM credentials never go in the request, and neither does the server the `openai` engine calls. Set them in the server's environment (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` for the server). See [Environment variables](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#environment-variables).

## ExecuteRequest

The body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/action`.

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | Required. Must be `"keyword"`. |
| `keyword` | string | The keyword. `"Press Element"` and `"press_element"` both work. |
| `params` | list or object | Positional values as a list, or named values as an object: `{"element": "text=Sign in"}`. A value can be a list of strings: Optics tries each one until the keyword passes. |
| `template_images` | object | `{"name": "<base64>"}` images available to this request only. |

The session has no elements file, so pass locators directly, or define variables first with keywords such as `Evaluate`.

## Responses

A successful action returns:

```json
{
  "execution_id": "4f1c2b7e-...",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "data": { "result": "Trail Runner 2" }
}
```

- When the keyword returns a value that isn't an object, `data` is `{"result": <value>}`.
- When the keyword returns an object, `data` is that object. This is why `/source` and `/screen_elements` put their fields directly in `data`.
- When self-heal recovers a step, `data` is `{"result", "healed": true, "heal_summary", "suggested_steps"}`. `suggested_steps` lists the keywords and parameters that fixed it.

Unlike `optics execute`, the HTTP API returns keyword results, so `Get Text`, `Assert Equality` and `Execute Script` values come back to you.

## Errors

| Status | When | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `mode` isn't `"keyword"`, a template image isn't valid base64, or `api_data` is invalid. | `{"detail": "<message>"}` |
| `404` | The session doesn't exist. | `{"detail": "Session not found"}` |
| `404` | The keyword doesn't exist. | `{"detail": {"type": "optics:keyword", "code": "Code.E0402", "status": 404, "message": "Keyword ... not found", ...}}` |
| `4xx`/`5xx` | Optics raised a coded error. The status depends on the code. | `{"detail": {"type", "code", "status", "message", "details", "meta"}}` |
| `500` | A keyword failed. | `{"detail": "Execution failed: All fallback attempts failed for keyword '...': ..."}`. The Optics code is inside the text. |
| `500` | The session couldn't start. | `{"detail": "Session creation failed: ..."}` or a coded error. |

- The `code` field can carry a `Code.` prefix, as in `Code.E0402`. It's the same code. See [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors).
- `DELETE /stop` on an unknown session returns 500 with `Session termination failed: 404: Session not found`.
- If closing the app fails during `DELETE /stop`, the session isn't removed. Call it again.

## Streams

Both stream endpoints use server-sent events (SSE): the connection stays open and each event is a `data:` line of JSON.

**`/events`** sends one event when each keyword starts, passes or fails, including the automatic `launch_app` at start, `close_and_terminate_app` at stop, and the GET helpers such as `/screenshot`.

```text
data: {"execution_id": "4f1c...", "status": "RUNNING", "message": "Starting keyword: press_element"}
data: {"execution_id": "4f1c...", "status": "SUCCESS", "message": "Keyword press_element executed successfully"}
```

- Statuses are `RUNNING`, `SUCCESS` and `FAIL`, plus `ERROR` or `CANCELLED` when the stream itself stops.
- After 15 seconds without events, it sends `{"execution_id": "heartbeat", "status": "HEARTBEAT", ...}`.
- Events wait in a queue until someone reads them. With several clients, each event goes to only one of them, so connect one client per session.

**`/workspace/stream`** sends the screen whenever it changes.

| Query | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `interval_ms` | `2000` | How often to check the screen. Minimum `500`. |
| `include_source` | `false` | Adds the UI tree or HTML as `source`. |
| `filter_config` | | Filters the elements, as for `/elements`. |

Each event is `{"screenshot", "elements", "screenshotFailed"}`, plus `source` when requested. It's sent only when the screen or elements change. Otherwise a `{"type": "heartbeat"}` arrives every 15 seconds, and errors arrive as `{"type": "error", "message"}`. The stream ends when the session ends.

## Walkthrough

This drives the Birch app on an Android emulator. You need an Appium server on port 4723 and the `appium` extra.

### Start the server

```shell
$ optics serve --port 8000
```

Leave it running and open a second terminal.

### Start a session

```shell
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/start \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"driver_sources": [{"appium": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:4723",
>          "capabilities": {"platformName": "Android", "automationName": "UiAutomator2",
>            "deviceName": "emulator-5554", "appPackage": "com.birch.shop",
>            "appActivity": "com.birch.shop.MainActivity"}}}],
>        "elements_sources": ["appium_find_element", "appium_page_source", "appium_screenshot"],
>        "text_detection": [], "image_detection": []}'
{"session_id":"8d0e7c55-...","driver_id":"...","status":"created"}
```

The app launches. Save the session id:

```shell
$ SID=8d0e7c55-...
```

### Watch events (optional)

In a third terminal:

```shell
$ curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/events
```

### Run keywords

```shell
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Press Element", "params": [["//*[@resource-id=\"com.birch.shop:id/search\"]", "text=Search"]]}'
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Enter Text", "params": {"element": "text=Search", "text": "Trail Runner 2"}}'
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Assert Presence", "params": ["text=Trail Runner 2", "20"]}'
```

The first call passes a list for `element`, so Optics tries the XPath and then the text.

### Save a screenshot

```shell
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/screenshot \
>   | python3 -c 'import sys,json,base64; open("screen.png","wb").write(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]["result"]))'
```

### End the session

```shell
$ curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/stop
{"status":"terminated"}
```

Optics writes `junit_output.xml` for the session to `execution_output/` in the project path, or in the folder where the server runs.

## Limits

- Sessions live in memory. Restarting the server ends them, and `optics live` and `optics mcp` can't see them.
- There's no record or save endpoint. Write the steps you ran into [project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files) to replay them with `optics execute`.
- Error detection doesn't run over HTTP.
- With the `ble` driver, the automatic `launch_app` at session start fails, because BLE can't launch apps.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors

# Error codes

> Learn what each Optics error code means and how to fix it.

When a step or command fails, Optics usually attaches a code such as `E0201`. The code tells you which part of Optics failed, and the message after it says why. This page lists every code in Optics 1.10.5 and what to do about each one.

## How codes are built

A code is a letter followed by four digits.

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| First letter | `E` is an error. `X` is an error after Optics tried every fallback or caught an exception. `W` is a warning. |
| First two digits | The family: `01` driver, `02` elements, `03` screenshots, `04` keywords, `05` files and config, `06` engines and modules, `07` test cases and variables, `08` general, `09` `optics live`. |
| Last two digits | The specific problem in that family. |

Codes in the `E02` family and `X0201` mean "element not found". When a step uses an element with fallback values, only these codes make Optics try the next value. Any other code fails the step straight away.

## Where codes appear

| Where | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| `optics execute` "Failure details" box | `<test> → step '<step>' — Keyword '<keyword>' failed: Code.E0401: <message>` |
| Log files (`file_log: true`) | The same reason as the Failure details box, as an error line in `execution_logs.log`. |
| `optics live` history | `✗ press_element ${sign_in}` with `[E0201] ...` on the line below |
| HTTP API (`optics serve`) | A `code` field in the error body, or the code inside a `detail` string. See [HTTP API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api#errors). |
| MCP server (`optics mcp`) | `[Code.E0106] Driver session is no longer active ...` in the tool error. See [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp#errors). |

In some places the code has a `Code.` prefix, as in `Code.E0102`. It's the same code. Search for the five characters, for example `E0102`.

Not every failure has a code. See [Messages without a code](#messages-without-a-code).

## E01: Driver and session

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0101` | **Driver not initialized.** A keyword ran before the driver session started. In `optics live` this happens when the automatic `launch_app` failed. | Start with `Launch App`. In `optics live`, run `launch_app` again and read its error first. |
| `E0102` | **Failed to start session.** The driver couldn't create a session. The Appium server refused it, Playwright couldn't open the browser, or the request took longer than 15 seconds. | Check that the server is running and the device is connected with `optics doctor <folder>`. Check the capabilities, especially `appPackage`, `appActivity` or `bundleId`. Read the Appium server's own log for the cause. |
| `E0104` | **Driver config incomplete.** A required driver setting is missing or wrong: empty Appium `capabilities`, no `platformName`, an unsupported `platformName`, or no server `url`. | Fill in the driver settings in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform). `platformName` must be `Android`, `iOS`, `TizenTV` or `LGTV`. |
| `E0105` | **Keyword not supported on this device platform.** You used a touch or typing keyword on a Samsung or LG TV, where Appium has no touch screen. | Navigate with `Press Keycode` and remote keys such as `UP`, `DOWN` and `ENTER`. See [Test TV apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv). |
| `E0106` | **Driver session is no longer active.** The Appium or Selenium server dropped the session, for example after a timeout, a device disconnect or a server restart. Optics doesn't reconnect. | Run the tests again. Over HTTP or MCP, end the session and start a new one. If it keeps happening, raise `newCommandTimeout` in the capabilities. |

## E02: Elements

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0201` | **Element not found.** No strategy found the element on the current screen. Also raised when a `${name}` variable isn't defined, when OCR is needed but no `text_detection` engine is enabled, or when `Scroll Until Element Appears` or `Swipe Until Element Appears` time out. | Check the locator against the screen with `optics live` or the page source. Put `Assert Presence` before the step if the element appears late, since actions don't wait. Add fallback values in `Element_ID_*` columns. Enable `easyocr` if you locate by visible text. |
| `X0201` | **Element not found after all fallbacks.** Optics found the element, or tried every fallback value, but the action failed each time. The element may be hidden, covered, disabled, or the wrong match. | Use `index` to pick the right match, an [area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest) to narrow the search, or a more specific locator. Turn on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal) for popups that get in the way. |
| `E0202` | **Unsupported operation for element source.** The enabled element sources can't do what the keyword asked, usually listing interactive elements. | Enable `appium_page_source` or `playwright_page_source`. Selenium can't list interactive elements; use the page source instead. |
| `E0205` | **Invalid element type.** An area of interest is out of range, or a `rule` isn't `any` or `all`. | Keep area values between 0 and 100, with `aoi_x + aoi_width` and `aoi_y + aoi_height` at most 100. Set `rule` to `any` or `all`. |

## E03: Screenshots

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0301` | **Screenshot disabled.** Optics tried to stop a screenshot stream that wasn't running. | Usually harmless. If it fails a step, rerun with `log_level: DEBUG` and report it. |
| `E0303` | **Screenshot empty or black.** Optics couldn't take a screenshot, got a black image, or has no screenshot source enabled. | Enable the screenshot source for your driver, such as `appium_screenshot`. Check that the device screen is on and unlocked. Some apps block screenshots on secure screens. |

## E04: Keywords and parameters

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0401` | **Action failed.** The keyword ran but couldn't complete: an app didn't launch, an element wasn't visible or enabled for `Is Element`, typing failed, a script failed, an API request failed, or a module run by `Run Loop`, `Condition` or `Execute Module` failed. In `optics live`, also shown for errors a keyword logged without failing. | Read the message after the code; it names the cause. For nested modules, the inner error is included. |
| `E0402` | **Keyword not found.** No keyword has that name. | Check the spelling with `optics list`. Case and spaces don't matter. |
